partner.hr: Onda ova slika nije samo tužna uspomena.
partner.en: Then this picture isn't only a sad memory.

learner.hr: Nije. Podsjeća me i na to koliko dobri ljudi mogu promijeniti nečiji život.
learner.en: No. It also reminds me how much good people can change someone's life.

conversations.title: Choosing costumes for a school show

partner.hr: Koju boju želiš za svoj kostim?
partner.en: What colour would you like for your costume?

learner.hr: Najradije bih plavu, ali učiteljica kaže da moj lik treba nositi bijelo.
learner.en: I'd prefer blue, but the teacher says my character needs to wear white.

partner.en: Why white specifically?

learner.hr: Zato što igram oblak, a druga djevojka igra sunce. Njezin kostim bit će žut.
learner.en: Because I'm playing a cloud, and another girl is playing the sun. Her costume will be yellow.

partner.hr: Možemo li na bijelu majicu dodati sive dijelove?
partner.en: Can we add grey pieces to a white shirt?

learner.hr: Možemo. Tako ću izgledati kao pravi kišni oblak, a ne kao obična kugla vate.
learner.en: Yes. That way I'll look like a real rain cloud rather than an ordinary ball of cotton wool.

partner.en: What would you like to put on your head?

learner.hr: Možda kapu s nekoliko plavih kapljica. Samo ne želim da mi prekrije lice.
learner.en: Maybe a hat with a few blue raindrops. I just don't want it to cover my face.

partner.hr: Hoćeš li i sam nešto izrezati?
partner.en: Would you like to cut some of it out yourself?

learner.hr: Hoću. Daj mi škare i pokazat ću ti kakav sam oblik zamislio.
learner.en: Yes. Give me the scissors, and I'll show you the shape I've imagined.

partner.en: Good, draw it on paper first.

learner.hr: Evo, ovako. Sad ovaj oblak ima više osobnosti nego svi ostali likovi zajedno.
learner.en: Here, like this. Now this cloud has more personality than all the other characters put together.

conversations.title: Preparing to host relatives from abroad

partner.hr: Kad dolaze tvoji rođaci iz Amerike?
partner.en: When are your relatives from America arriving?

learner.hr: Njihov avion slijeće sutra ujutro. Idem po njih na aerodrom.
learner.en: Their plane lands tomorrow morning. I'm going to pick them up at the airport.

partner.en: Do they speak Croatian?

learner.hr: Malo. Njihova majka govori odlično, ali djeca uglavnom govore engleski.
learner.en: A little. Their mother speaks it very well, but the children mostly speak English.

partner.hr: Kako ćete se sporazumjeti s bakom?
partner.en: How will they communicate with Grandma?

learner.hr: Ona zna nekoliko engleskih riječi, a mi ćemo prevesti ono što ne razumiju.
learner.en: She knows a few English words, and we'll translate what they don't understand.

partner.en: Have they been here before?

learner.hr: Njihov otac jest, ali oni nisu. Žele vidjeti selo iz kojeg je obitelj otišla prije mnogo godina.
learner.en: Their father has, but they haven't. They want to see the village their family left many years ago.

partner.hr: Hoćete li im pokazati i obalu?
partner.en: Will you show them the coast too?

learner.hr: Hoćemo. Najprije ćemo se odmoriti od puta, a onda ih vodimo na more.
learner.en: Yes. First we'll recover from the journey, and then we're taking them to the seaside.

partner.en: I'm sure they'll find it interesting.

learner.hr: Nadam se. Baka već priprema toliko hrane kao da dolazi pola Amerike.
learner.en: I hope so. Grandma's already preparing enough food for half of America.

conversations.title: An interview for the school newspaper

partner.hr: Mogu li te intervjuirati za školske novine?
partner.en: Can I interview you for the school newspaper?

learner.hr: Možeš, ali nisam sigurna da sam dovoljno zanimljiva za cijeli članak.
learner.en: Yes, but I'm not sure I'm interesting enough for a whole article.

partner.hr: Pobijedila si na natjecanju iz robotike.
partner.en: You won the robotics competition.

learner.hr: Jesam, ali nisam radila sama. Naš tim ima četiri člana i svi zaslužuju spomen.
learner.en: Yes, but I didn't work alone. Our team has four members, and everyone deserves a mention.

partner.hr: Onda bih mogao razgovarati sa svima vama.
partner.en: Then I could talk to all of you.

learner.hr: To bi bilo pravednije. Marko je osmislio dizajn, a ostali su radili na programu i izradi.
learner.en: That would be fairer. Marko came up with the design, and the others worked on the software and construction.

partner.en: What was the hardest part?

learner.hr: Prihvatiti neuspjeh kad prvi pokušaj nije uspio. Mislili smo da je sav trud bio uzaludan.
learner.en: Accepting failure when the first attempt didn't work. We thought all our effort had been wasted.

partner.en: How did you carry on despite that?

learner.hr: Profesor nam je pomogao pronaći pogrešku, ali nije obavio posao umjesto nas.
learner.en: The teacher helped us find the mistake, but he didn't do the work for us.

partner.hr: To je odličan završetak za članak.
partner.en: That's a great ending for the article.

learner.hr: Samo nam ga pokaži prije nego što ga objaviš, da provjerimo imena i tehničke detalje.
learner.en: Just show it to us before you publish it, so we can check the names and technical details.

conversations.title: Finding a comfortable way to exercise

partner.hr: Kako je prošao prvi posjet teretani?
partner.en: How did your first visit to the gym go?

learner.hr: Bio sam nervozan jer nisam znao koristiti nijedan aparat.
learner.en: I was nervous because I didn't know how to use any of the machines.

partner.en: Did someone show you?

learner.hr: Jest, trener mi je sve polako objasnio i pitao čime se inače bavim.
learner.en: Yes, a trainer explained everything slowly and asked what activities I usually do.

partner.en: What did you tell him?

learner.hr: Da uglavnom sjedim na poslu i da se želim više kretati, bez natjecanja s drugima.
learner.en: That I mostly sit at work and want to move more, without competing with other people.

partner.hr: Je li ti bilo neugodno pred ostalima?
partner.en: Did you feel awkward around everyone else?

learner.hr: Isprva jest, ali nitko nije gledao u mene. Ljudi su bili zauzeti svojim vježbama.
learner.en: At first, yes, but nobody was staring at me. People were busy doing their own exercises.

partner.en: Will you go back?

learner.hr: Hoću, ali radije ujutro kad nije gužva. Tad se lakše usredotočim na ono što radim.
learner.en: Yes, but preferably in the morning when it's less busy. It's easier to focus on what I'm doing then.

partner.en: Can I join you?

learner.hr: Naravno. Bit će mi drago imati društvo, samo me nemoj pretvoriti u svog natjecatelja.
learner.en: Of course. I'd be glad of the company; just don't turn me into your competitor.

conversations.title: Returning a costume with a missing button

partner.hr: Vraćate li kostim koji ste unajmili?
partner.en: Are you returning the costume you hired?

learner.hr: Da, ali prije nego što ga pregledate, moram vam nešto reći.
learner.en: Yes, but before you inspect it, I need to tell you something.

partner.en: Was anything damaged?

learner.hr: Na kaputu nedostaje jedan gumb. Otpao je tijekom predstave i nisam ga uspio pronaći.
learner.en: One button is missing from the coat. It fell off during the performance, and I couldn't find it.

partner.en: The rest looks tidy.

learner.hr: Pazio sam na njega. Nisam ga pokušao sam popraviti jer nisam htio napraviti veću štetu.
learner.en: I took care of it. I didn't try to repair it myself because I didn't want to cause more damage.

partner.hr: Imamo zamjenske gumbe za taj model.
partner.en: We have spare buttons for that model.

learner.hr: To je olakšanje. Recite mi trebam li platiti popravak ili donijeti nešto drugo.
learner.en: That's a relief. Tell me if I need to pay for the repair or bring anything else.

partner.en: That won't be necessary in this case.

learner.hr: Hvala vam. Cijenim to što niste napravili problem od male nezgode.
learner.en: Thank you. I appreciate you not making a problem out of a small mishap.

partner.en: How did the play go?

learner.hr: Odlično. Moj lik izgubio je kraljevstvo, a ja sam, srećom, izgubio samo gumb.
learner.en: Very well. My character lost his kingdom, and fortunately I only lost a button.

conversations.title: A photograph used with the wrong caption

partner.hr: Zašto si uzrujan zbog današnjih novina?
partner.en: Why are you upset about today's newspaper?

learner.hr: Objavili su moju fotografiju uz članak o nesreći s kojom nemam nikakve veze.
learner.en: They published my photo next to an article about an accident I have nothing to do with.

partner.en: How did that happen?

learner.hr: Ne znam. Fotograf je snimio našu ulicu prošli tjedan, a na slici sam slučajno i ja.
learner.en: I don't know. A photographer took a picture of our street last week, and I happen to be in it.

partner.en: Have you spoken to the editor?

learner.hr: Poslao sam poruku redakciji i zamolio ih da isprave opis ispod slike.
learner.en: I sent a message to the editorial team and asked them to correct the caption under the picture.

partner.en: Have they replied?

learner.hr: Jesu. Kažu da je riječ o pogrešci pri odabiru fotografije i da će objaviti ispravak.
learner.en: Yes. They say the wrong photo was selected by mistake and that they'll publish a correction.

partner.hr: Hoćeš li im još što napisati?
partner.en: Will you write anything else to them?

learner.hr: Zamolit ću ih da uklone pogrešnu sliku i s interneta. Ne želim da se nesporazum širi.
learner.en: I'll ask them to remove the wrong picture from the internet too. I don't want the misunderstanding to spread.

partner.hr: Dobro je da si reagirao mirno.
partner.en: It's good that you responded calmly.

learner.hr: Trudim se. Ljutit razgovor ne bi pomogao ni meni ni njima da riješimo problem.
learner.en: I'm trying. An angry conversation wouldn't help either of us solve the problem.

conversations.title: A model ship in a museum

partner.hr: Zašto se toliko zadržavaš kod tog modela?
partner.en: Why are you spending so long at that model?

learner.hr: Moj djed radio je na sličnom brodu. Zanima me kako su mornari tada živjeli.
learner.en: My grandfather worked on a similar ship. I'm interested in how sailors lived back then.

partner.hr: Jesu li plovili i preko oceana?
partner.en: Did they sail across the ocean too?

learner.hr: Jesu. Na ovim fotografijama vidiš luku iz koje su odlazili i članove posade na palubi.
learner.en: Yes. These photographs show the port they left from and crew members on deck.

partner.en: Where did the captain sleep?

learner.hr: Pretpostavljam da je imao vlastitu kabinu, ali trebamo pogledati plan broda da budemo sigurni.
learner.en: I assume he had his own cabin, but we should look at the ship's plan to be sure.

partner.hr: Ovdje piše da je brod potonuo.
partner.en: It says here that the ship sank.

learner.hr: Da, tijekom oluje. Posada je spašena, ali brod nikad nije izvučen s dna.
learner.en: Yes, during a storm. The crew was rescued, but the ship was never raised from the seabed.

partner.hr: Je li tvoj djed tada bio na njemu?
partner.en: Was your grandfather aboard at the time?

learner.hr: Nije. Već je radio na kopnu kad se to dogodilo, ali poznavao je neke mornare.
learner.en: No. He was already working on land when it happened, but he knew some of the sailors.

partner.hr: Sad razumijem zašto te izložba zanima.
partner.en: Now I understand why you're interested in the exhibition.

learner.hr: Volio bih da sam ga više pitao o tim putovanjima dok je još bio živ.
learner.en: I wish I'd asked him more about those journeys while he was still alive.

conversations.title: Deciding what to do with a family house

partner.hr: Jesi li razmislio što ćemo s kućom?
partner.en: Have you thought about what we'll do with the house?

learner.hr: Jesam, ali ne želim odlučiti bez tebe. Obojica imamo uspomene vezane uz nju.
learner.en: Yes, but I don't want to decide without you. Both of us have memories connected to it.

partner.hr: Meni je teško zamisliti da je prodamo.
partner.en: I find it hard to imagine selling it.

learner.hr: I meni. Ipak, održavanje puno košta, a nijedan od nas ne živi blizu.
learner.en: Me too. Still, maintenance costs a lot, and neither of us lives nearby.

partner.en: Maybe we could rent it out.

learner.hr: To je jedna mogućnost. Najprije bismo trebali saznati koliko bi popravci koštali.
learner.en: That's one possibility. First we should find out how much the repairs would cost.

partner.hr: Zamolit ću susjeda da nam preporuči majstora.
partner.en: I'll ask the neighbour to recommend a tradesperson.

learner.hr: Dobro. Ja ću prikupiti račune pa ćemo vidjeti koliki su godišnji troškovi.
learner.en: Good. I'll gather the bills so we can see what the annual costs are.

partner.hr: Ne želim da nas novac posvađa.
partner.en: I don't want money to cause an argument between us.

learner.hr: Ne želim ni ja. Naš odnos važniji mi je od bilo koje nekretnine.
learner.en: Neither do I. Our relationship matters more to me than any property.

partner.en: Then let's take it one step at a time.

learner.hr: Dogovoreno. Ne moramo sve riješiti danas niti se odreći svih mogućnosti unaprijed.
learner.en: Agreed. We don't have to solve everything today or rule out every option in advance.

conversations.title: A science project that failed honestly

partner.en: Did your experiment work?

learner.hr: Nije dao rezultat koji sam očekivao. Biljke u sjeni rasle su drukčije nego što sam pretpostavio.
learner.en: It didn't give the result I expected. The plants in the shade grew differently from what I'd assumed.

partner.en: Will you repeat the measurements?

learner.hr: Hoću, ali prvo moram zapisati sve što se dogodilo, uključujući pogreške.
learner.en: Yes, but first I need to write down everything that happened, including the mistakes.

partner.en: What mistakes?

learner.hr: Jednu sam biljku zalio dvaput, a drugoj nisam dao dovoljno vode. To utječe na usporedbu.
learner.en: I watered one plant twice and didn't give another enough water. That affects the comparison.

partner.hr: Možeš li taj dio izostaviti iz izvještaja?
partner.en: Could you leave that part out of the report?

learner.hr: Ne bih smio. Analiza nema smisla ako sakrijem podatke koji mi se ne sviđaju.
learner.en: I shouldn't. The analysis is meaningless if I hide the data I don't like.

partner.hr: Misliš da će profesor to cijeniti?
partner.en: Do you think the teacher will appreciate that?

learner.hr: Nadam se. Cilj nije dokazati da sam uvijek u pravu, nego naučiti kako provjeriti svoju ideju.
learner.en: I hope so. The aim isn't to prove I'm always right, but to learn how to test my idea.

partner.en: Then can the title stay the same?

learner.hr: Može, samo ću u zaključku jasno objasniti ograničenja i što bih sljedeći put promijenio.
learner.en: Yes; I'll just clearly explain the limitations in the conclusion and what I'd change next time.

conversations.title: Trying out for community radio

partner.hr: Kako je prošla audicija za radio?
partner.en: How did the radio audition go?

learner.hr: Iznenađujuće dobro. Mislila sam da će mi glas drhtati, ali nakon prve minute sam se opustila.
learner.en: Surprisingly well. I thought my voice would shake, but I relaxed after the first minute.

partner.en: What did they give you to read?

learner.hr: Kratke vijesti i najavu jedne emisije. Zatim su me pitali koju glazbu volim.
learner.en: Short news items and an introduction to a programme. Then they asked what music I like.

partner.en: Did they comment on your reading?

learner.hr: Rekli su da govorim jasno, ali prebrzo. Trebam ostaviti više prostora između rečenica.
learner.en: They said I speak clearly, but too fast. I need to leave more space between sentences.

partner.en: Will you get your own programme?

learner.hr: Ne odmah. Najprije ću pomagati iskusnijoj voditeljici i naučiti kako radi oprema.
learner.en: Not straight away. First I'll help a more experienced presenter and learn how the equipment works.

partner.en: Would you like to interview musicians?

learner.hr: Bih. Naš grad ima zanimljivih bendova, a malo ljudi zna njihove priče.
learner.en: Yes. Our city has interesting bands, but few people know their stories.

partner.hr: Javi mi kad prvi put budeš u programu.
partner.en: Let me know when you're on air for the first time.

learner.hr: Hoću, ali nemoj okupiti cijelu obitelj pred radijem. To bi me tek učinilo nervoznom.
learner.en: I will, but don't gather the whole family around the radio. That really would make me nervous.

conversations.title: Choosing something useful for new parents

partner.hr: Što ćemo odnijeti prijateljima za bebu?
partner.en: What shall we take our friends for the baby?

learner.hr: Radije bih nešto korisno nego još jednu ogromnu igračku.
learner.en: I'd rather take something useful than another enormous toy.

partner.en: Maybe clothes?

learner.hr: Možda, ali ne znam koju veličinu nose bebe u toj dobi. Bolje da prvo pitamo roditelje.
learner.en: Maybe, but I don't know what size babies that age wear. We'd better ask the parents first.

partner.en: Wouldn't that spoil the surprise?

learner.hr: Hoće, ali važnije mi je da im dar stvarno pomogne nego da ih iznenadi.
learner.en: Yes, but it's more important to me that the gift actually helps them than that it surprises them.

partner.en: We could cook them dinner.

learner.hr: To je dobra ideja. Njihova djevojčica slabo spava pa ni oni nemaju puno odmora.
learner.en: That's a good idea. Their little girl doesn't sleep much, so they don't get much rest either.

partner.hr: Hoćemo li ostati jesti s njima?
partner.en: Shall we stay and eat with them?

learner.hr: Samo ako to žele. Možemo ostaviti hranu i otići, bez očekivanja da nas ugoste.
learner.en: Only if they want us to. We can drop off the food and leave without expecting them to host us.

partner.hr: Poslat ću im poruku da pitam.
partner.en: I'll send them a message and ask.

learner.hr: Super. Napiši da nema obaveze odgovarati odmah i da ćemo se prilagoditi njihovom rasporedu.
learner.en: Great. Say there's no pressure to reply straight away and that we'll fit around their schedule.

conversations.title: A missing guitar and a mistaken suspicion

partner.hr: Jesi li pronašao gitaru nakon probe?
partner.en: Did you find your guitar after rehearsal?

learner.hr: Jesam. Bila je u drugoj prostoriji, iza velikog zvučnika.
learner.en: Yes. It was in the other room, behind a large speaker.

partner.hr: A mislio si da ju je Luka uzeo.
partner.en: And you thought Luka had taken it.

learner.hr: Znam i sad me je sram. Optužio sam ga bez ikakvog dokaza.
learner.en: I know, and now I'm ashamed. I accused him without any evidence.

partner.en: Have you apologised to him?

learner.hr: Jesam, ali razumijem da je još ljut. Rekao sam nešto što ga je povrijedilo.
learner.en: Yes, but I understand that he's still angry. I said something that hurt him.

partner.hr: Zašto si odmah pomislio na njega?
partner.en: Why did you immediately think of him?

learner.hr: Zato što smo se prije toga posvađali. Dopustio sam da moj bijes zamijeni razmišljanje.
learner.en: Because we'd argued earlier. I let my anger take the place of thinking.

partner.en: Maybe he needs a little time.

learner.hr: Dat ću mu ga. Ne mogu očekivati da mi oprosti čim meni postane neugodno.
learner.en: I'll give him that. I can't expect him to forgive me as soon as I start feeling uncomfortable.

partner.hr: Što ćeš učiniti ako se vrati na probu?
partner.en: What will you do if he returns to rehearsal?

learner.hr: Ponašat ću se prema njemu s poštovanjem i sljedeći put provjeriti činjenice prije optužbe.
learner.en: I'll treat him with respect and check the facts before making an accusation next time.

conversations.title: A class visit to a museum

partner.en: Why are the pupils waiting outside the doors?

learner.hr: Muzej još nije otvoren za grupe. Naša učiteljica upravo razgovara s vodičem.
learner.en: The museum isn't open to groups yet. Our teacher is speaking to the guide now.

partner.en: Has everyone brought their tickets?

learner.hr: Jesu. Ja čuvam njihove ulaznice u ovoj kuverti da ih netko ne izgubi.
learner.en: Yes. I'm keeping their tickets in this envelope so nobody loses them.

partner.hr: Trebamo li im objasniti pravila prije ulaska?
partner.en: Should we explain the rules before going in?

learner.hr: Trebamo. Posebno da ne smiju dirati predmete niti trčati između vitrina.
learner.en: Yes. Especially that they mustn't touch the objects or run between the display cases.

partner.hr: Mogu li postavljati pitanja tijekom obilaska?
partner.en: Can they ask questions during the tour?

learner.hr: Naravno. Želimo da budu znatiželjni, a ne samo tihi i poslušni.
learner.en: Of course. We want them to be curious, not just quiet and obedient.

partner.en: How long are we staying inside?

learner.hr: Oko sat vremena. Poslije imamo stanku za obrok u dvorištu.
learner.en: About an hour. Afterwards we have a meal break in the courtyard.

partner.en: The guide is waving us in; we can go inside.

learner.hr: Odlično. Ja ću ostati zadnja da provjerim da nitko nije ostao ispred zgrade.
learner.en: Great. I'll stay at the back to check that nobody's been left outside the building.

conversations.title: A choir solo that feels unfair

partner.hr: Zašto si otišla odmah nakon probe?
partner.en: Why did you leave straight after rehearsal?

learner.hr: Bila sam razočarana što nisam dobila solo, pa nisam htjela pred svima plakati.
learner.en: I was disappointed I hadn't got the solo, and I didn't want to cry in front of everyone.

partner.hr: Misliš li da je izbor bio nepravedan?
partner.en: Do you think the choice was unfair?

learner.hr: Ne znam. Ana pjeva odlično, ali nadala sam se da ću ovaj put dobiti priliku.
learner.en: I don't know. Ana sings beautifully, but I'd hoped I'd get a chance this time.

partner.hr: Jesi li pitala voditelja za povratnu informaciju?
partner.en: Have you asked the conductor for feedback?

learner.hr: Nisam još. Trebalo mi je vremena da odvojim svoju tugu od procjene njezina pjevanja.
learner.en: Not yet. I needed time to separate my sadness from my judgement of her singing.

partner.hr: To ne znači da moraš odustati.
partner.en: That doesn't mean you have to give up.

learner.hr: Znam. Želim naučiti što mogu poboljšati, a ne pretvarati prijateljicu u neprijatelja.
learner.en: I know. I want to learn what I can improve rather than turn a friend into an enemy.

partner.hr: Hoćeš li doći na sljedeću probu?
partner.en: Will you come to the next rehearsal?

learner.hr: Hoću. I čestitat ću Ani, jer njezin uspjeh ne umanjuje sav moj trud.
learner.en: Yes. And I'll congratulate Ana, because her success doesn't diminish all my effort.

partner.en: I'm glad to hear that.

learner.hr: I meni je lakše kad ovo kažem naglas. Ne moram skrivati osjećaje da bih bila dobra prijateljica.
learner.en: I feel better saying it aloud too. I don't have to hide my feelings to be a good friend.

conversations.title: An incomplete family recipe

partner.hr: Možeš li pročitati što ovdje piše?
partner.en: Can you read what this says?

learner.hr: Jedva. Bakina bilježnica ima mrlju baš preko količine brašna.
learner.en: Barely. Grandma's notebook has a stain right over the amount of flour.

partner.hr: Sjećaš li se kako je radila taj kolač?
partner.en: Do you remember how she made that cake?

learner.hr: Sjećam se velike bijele zdjele i drvene žlice, ali ne i točnih mjera.
learner.en: I remember a large white bowl and a wooden spoon, but not the exact quantities.

partner.en: Maybe our aunt knows the recipe.

learner.hr: Nazvala sam je. Kaže da je baka uvijek govorila da se brašna doda koliko treba.
learner.en: I called her. She says Grandma always said to add as much flour as needed.

partner.en: That doesn't really help us.

learner.hr: Ne pomaže, ali barem znamo kakav okus tražimo. Možemo napraviti malu probnu smjesu.
learner.en: No, but at least we know what taste we're looking for. We can make a small test batch.

partner.en: And if it doesn't work?

learner.hr: Onda ćemo pokušati ponovno i zapisati što smo promijenili, umjesto da se pretvaramo da znamo.
learner.en: Then we'll try again and write down what we changed instead of pretending we know.

partner.en: Agreed. Where are the ingredients?

learner.hr: Maslac je u hladnjaku, jaja su na stolu, a naša hrabrost valjda negdje između.
learner.en: The butter's in the fridge, the eggs are on the table, and our courage is somewhere in between, I suppose.

conversations.title: Sharing volunteer work more fairly

partner.hr: Možeš li preuzeti još jednu smjenu u subotu?
partner.en: Can you take another shift on Saturday?

learner.hr: Žao mi je, ali ovaj put ne mogu. Već sam preuzela više nego što mogu obaviti.
learner.en: I'm sorry, but I can't this time. I've already taken on more than I can manage.

partner.hr: Nemamo nikoga drugog za taj termin.
partner.en: We don't have anyone else for that time.

learner.hr: Razumijem, ali nije održivo da uvijek isti ljudi popunjavaju sve praznine.
learner.en: I understand, but it's not sustainable for the same people to keep filling every gap.

partner.en: What do you suggest?

learner.hr: Mogli bismo poslati raspored svima i jasno napisati koje su smjene još slobodne.
learner.en: We could send the rota to everyone and clearly list which shifts are still free.

partner.en: Some people won't volunteer on their own.

learner.hr: Onda ih možemo osobno pitati, bez pritiska. Možda ne znaju da nam nedostaje pomoć.
learner.en: Then we can ask them personally, without pressure. Maybe they don't know we're short of help.

partner.hr: Hoćeš li mi pomoći napisati poruku?
partner.en: Will you help me write the message?

learner.hr: Hoću. To mogu napraviti danas, ali u subotu moram ostati pri svom dogovoru s obitelji.
learner.en: Yes. I can do that today, but on Saturday I need to keep my arrangement with my family.

partner.hr: U redu, hvala što si iskrena.
partner.en: All right, thank you for being honest.

learner.hr: Hvala tebi što razumiješ. Želim pomagati dugo, a ne izgorjeti nakon nekoliko mjeseci.
learner.en: Thank you for understanding. I want to keep helping for a long time rather than burn out after a few months.

conversations.title: A neighbour waters the wrong plants

partner.hr: Kako su biljke preživjele dok me nije bilo?
partner.en: How did the plants survive while I was away?

learner.hr: Većina dobro, ali moram priznati da sam jednu stvar krivo razumio.
learner.en: Most are fine, but I have to admit I misunderstood one thing.

partner.en: What happened?

learner.hr: Zalijevao sam i onu plastičnu biljku na donjoj polici. Tek sam jučer primijetio da nema zemlje.
learner.en: I watered the plastic plant on the lower shelf too. I only noticed yesterday that it had no soil.

partner.hr: Nisi valjda? Ona je godinama ista.
partner.en: You didn't! It's looked the same for years.

learner.hr: Sad mi je jasno zašto je uvijek izgledala tako zdravo. Mislio sam da imaš poseban dar za biljke.
learner.en: Now I understand why it always looked so healthy. I thought you had a special gift with plants.

partner.hr: Jesi li barem obrisao vodu ispod nje?
partner.en: Did you at least wipe up the water underneath it?

learner.hr: Jesam. Maknuo sam lonac, osušio policu i provjerio da ništa nije oštećeno.
learner.en: Yes. I moved the pot, dried the shelf and checked that nothing was damaged.

partner.en: Then there's no harm done.

learner.hr: Osim mog ponosa. Molim te, nemoj ovu priču ispričati svim susjedima.
learner.en: Apart from to my pride. Please don't tell all the neighbours this story.

partner.en: I promise; it'll stay between us.

learner.hr: Hvala. Sljedeći put mi ostavi pisane upute, uključujući popis biljaka koje zapravo nisu žive.
learner.en: Thanks. Next time, leave me written instructions, including a list of the plants that aren't actually alive.

conversations.title: Planning a holiday within a budget

partner.hr: Jesi li pogledao smještaj koji sam poslala?
partner.en: Have you looked at the accommodation I sent you?

learner.hr: Jesam. Izgleda divno, ali ukupna cijena veća je nego što smo planirali.
learner.en: Yes. It looks lovely, but the total price is more than we'd planned.

partner.en: Maybe we could stay for less time.

learner.hr: Mogli bismo, ali onda bismo većinu odmora proveli na putu.
learner.en: We could, but then we'd spend most of the holiday travelling.

partner.hr: Želiš li odustati od tog mjesta?
partner.en: Do you want to give up on that place?

learner.hr: Ne nužno. Možda postoji skromniji apartman dalje od plaže, pa bismo svaki dan malo hodali.
learner.en: Not necessarily. Maybe there's a simpler apartment farther from the beach, and we could walk a little each day.

partner.hr: To mi ne smeta ako nije uz prometnu cestu.
partner.en: I don't mind that if it isn't beside a busy road.

learner.hr: Slažem se. Bolje mirna ulica i obična soba nego luksuz u kojem se ne možemo opustiti.
learner.en: I agree. A quiet street and an ordinary room are better than luxury we can't relax in.

partner.hr: Koliko novca želimo ostaviti za izlete?
partner.en: How much money do we want to leave for excursions?

learner.hr: Dovoljno za jedan brodski izlet i nekoliko ulaznica. Ne moramo svaki dan nešto plaćati.
learner.en: Enough for one boat trip and a few admission tickets. We don't need to pay for an activity every day.

partner.hr: Onda ću potražiti još nekoliko mogućnosti.
partner.en: Then I'll look for a few more options.

learner.hr: Dobro. Želim se vratiti s lijepim uspomenama, a ne s dugom zbog kojeg ćemo se brinuti.
learner.en: Good. I want to come back with happy memories rather than a debt we'll worry about.

conversations.title: A cover for a fantasy novel

partner.hr: Što želiš na naslovnici svoje knjige?
partner.en: What would you like on the cover of your book?

learner.hr: Stari dvorac iznad doline, nekoliko oblaka i malog zmaja koji se skriva iza kule.
learner.en: An old castle above a valley, a few clouds and a little dragon hiding behind a tower.

partner.hr: Treba li se vidjeti glavni junak?
partner.en: Should the main character be visible?

learner.hr: Ne mora. Važnije mi je da slika stvori tajanstvenu atmosferu, bez otkrivanja previše detalja.
learner.en: Not necessarily. It's more important that the picture creates a mysterious atmosphere without revealing too much detail.

partner.en: Is the dragon dangerous?

learner.hr: Na početku svi misle da jest, ali zapravo pokušava zaštititi svoje mladunce od ljudi.
learner.en: At first everyone thinks so, but it's actually trying to protect its young from people.

partner.hr: Onda ga ne bih nacrtala kako napada selo.
partner.en: Then I wouldn't draw it attacking the village.

learner.hr: Slažem se. To bi stvorilo pogrešan dojam o priči i pretvorilo ga u običnog neprijatelja.
learner.en: I agree. That would give the wrong impression of the story and turn it into an ordinary enemy.

partner.hr: Želiš li svijetle ili tamne boje?
partner.en: Would you like light or dark colours?

learner.hr: Tamne u pozadini, ali malo svjetla na prozorima. U priči postoji opasnost, ali i nada.
learner.en: Dark ones in the background, but a little light in the windows. There's danger in the story, but also hope.

partner.hr: Napravit ću dvije skice pa ćemo usporediti.
partner.en: I'll make two sketches, and we'll compare them.

learner.hr: Odlično. Veselim se vidjeti kako će netko drugi zamisliti svijet koji je dosad bio samo u mojoj glavi.
learner.en: Great. I'm looking forward to seeing how someone else imagines a world that's existed only in my head until now.

conversations.title: Questions after a planetarium show

partner.hr: Što ti se najviše svidjelo u planetariju?
partner.en: What did you like most at the planetarium?

learner.hr: Prizor zvijezda iznad naših glava. Na trenutak sam imao osjećaj da stvarno putujemo svemirom.
learner.en: The sight of the stars above our heads. For a moment I felt as though we were really travelling through space.

partner.hr: Jesi li razumio sve što je voditelj objašnjavao?
partner.en: Did you understand everything the presenter explained?

learner.hr: Nisam. Dio o udaljenostima bio mi je težak, jer ne mogu zamisliti tako velike brojeve.
learner.en: No. I found the part about distances difficult because I can't imagine such large numbers.

partner.hr: Možda možemo nešto pročitati o tome kod kuće.
partner.en: Maybe we can read about it at home.

learner.hr: Možemo. Zanima me i kako znanstvenici proučavaju svemir kad ne mogu otići do svake zvijezde.
learner.en: Yes. I'm also interested in how scientists study the universe when they can't visit every star.

partner.hr: U trgovini imaju knjigu s jednostavnim objašnjenjima.
partner.en: The shop has a book with simple explanations.

learner.hr: Pogledajmo je. Samo ne želim knjigu koja izmišlja odgovore na pitanja koja još nitko nije riješio.
learner.en: Let's look at it. I just don't want a book that invents answers to questions nobody has solved yet.

partner.hr: Zašto ti je to toliko važno?
partner.en: Why does that matter so much to you?

learner.hr: Zato što mi je zanimljivije znati što se stvarno zna, a što je zasad samo teorija ili pretpostavka.
learner.en: Because I find it more interesting to know what's actually known and what's still just a theory or assumption.

partner.hr: Onda ćemo pitati voditelja za preporuku.
partner.en: Then we'll ask the presenter for a recommendation.

learner.hr: Odlično. Možda je ovo početak mog novog hobija, a ne samo jednog školskog izleta.
learner.en: Great. Maybe this is the start of a new hobby for me rather than just one school trip.

conversations.title: Rehearsing a courtroom scene

partner.en: What part do you have in the play?

learner.hr: Igram suca. Veći dio radnje odvija se u sudnici tijekom izmišljenog suđenja.
learner.en: I play the judge. Most of the action takes place in a courtroom during a fictional trial.

partner.en: Do you have a lot of lines to learn?

learner.hr: Moram, a teško mi je zapamtiti redoslijed. Prvo govori odvjetnica, zatim svjedok, pa tek onda ja.
learner.en: Yes, and I find the order hard to remember. First the lawyer speaks, then the witness, and only then me.

partner.hr: Hoćeš li da ti čitam ostale uloge?
partner.en: Would you like me to read the other parts?

learner.hr: To bi mi pomoglo. Kad preskočim nečiju rečenicu, više ne znam na što trebam odgovoriti.
learner.en: That would help. When I skip someone else's line, I no longer know what I'm supposed to respond to.

partner.en: Where do we start?

learner.hr: Ovdje, gdje optuženi kaže da je nevin, a svjedoci se ne slažu oko onoga što su vidjeli.
learner.en: Here, where the accused says he's innocent and the witnesses disagree about what they saw.

partner.en: Should you speak sternly?

learner.hr: Na početku da, ali ne cijelo vrijeme. Redatelj želi da gledatelji vide i moju sumnju.
learner.en: At first, yes, but not all the time. The director wants the audience to see my doubts too.

partner.en: All right, let's start from this page.

learner.hr: Hvala. Ako slučajno kažem tvoje ime umjesto imena lika, nemoj me odmah izbaciti iz vlastite sudnice.
learner.en: Thanks. If I accidentally say your name instead of the character's, don't throw me out of my own courtroom straight away.

conversations.title: Waiting out a power cut with neighbours

partner.en: Have you got electricity?

learner.hr: Nema. Svjetla su se ugasila prije nekoliko minuta i dizalo je stalo.
learner.en: No. The lights went out a few minutes ago, and the lift stopped.

partner.en: Is anyone stuck inside?

learner.hr: Koliko znamo, nije. Susjed je upravo razgovarao s upraviteljem zgrade.
learner.en: Not as far as we know. The neighbour has just spoken to the building manager.

partner.hr: Zna li se kad će popraviti kvar?
partner.en: Do they know when the fault will be fixed?

learner.hr: Još ne. Obavijestit će nas kad dobiju točnije podatke. Zasad ne želim nagađati.
learner.en: Not yet. They'll tell us when they have more precise information. I don't want to guess for now.

partner.en: I've got a torch if you need one.

learner.hr: Hvala, imam i ja jednu. Više me brine susjeda na petom katu jer teško ide stepenicama.
learner.en: Thanks; I've got one too. I'm more worried about the neighbour on the fifth floor because she struggles with the stairs.

partner.hr: Mogu je nazvati da provjerim treba li što.
partner.en: I can call to check whether she needs anything.

learner.hr: To bi bilo lijepo. Ako želi društvo, možemo joj odnijeti čaj i malo sjediti s njom.
learner.en: That would be kind. If she'd like company, we could take her some tea and sit with her for a while.

partner.hr: Kaže da bi joj to baš odgovaralo.
partner.en: She says she'd really like that.

learner.hr: Onda idemo polako. Nisam planirao večernje druženje u mraku, ali barem nitko neće gledati televiziju.
learner.en: Then let's take our time going up. I hadn't planned an evening visit in the dark, but at least nobody will be watching television.

conversations.title: A disputed football decision

partner.hr: Zašto se još ljutiš zbog utakmice?
partner.en: Why are you still angry about the match?

learner.hr: Mislim da je sudac pogriješio kod zadnjeg gola. Činilo mi se da je lopta izašla izvan terena.
learner.en: I think the referee made a mistake with the last goal. It looked to me as though the ball had gone out of play.

partner.en: Have you watched the recording?

learner.hr: Jesam, ali ni na njoj se ne vidi jasno. Kamera je bila na suprotnoj strani.
learner.en: Yes, but it isn't clear there either. The camera was on the opposite side.

partner.hr: Onda možda nije mogao donijeti bolju odluku.
partner.en: Then perhaps he couldn't have made a better decision.

learner.hr: Možda. Ipak, teško je prihvatiti poraz kad misliš da si izgubio zbog nečije pogreške.
learner.en: Perhaps. Still, it's hard to accept defeat when you think you've lost because of someone's mistake.

partner.hr: Vaša je obrana i prije toga imala problema.
partner.en: Your defence had problems before that too.

learner.hr: Istina. Propustili smo nekoliko prilika i ne možemo svu krivnju prebaciti na njega.
learner.en: True. We missed several chances, and we can't put all the blame on him.

partner.hr: Hoćeš li ipak doći na sljedeću utakmicu?
partner.en: Will you still come to the next match?

learner.hr: Naravno. Volim nogomet i svoj klub, čak i kad se vratim kući loše volje.
learner.en: Of course. I love football and my club, even when I go home in a bad mood.

partner.en: Then I'll see you on Saturday.

learner.hr: Vidimo se. Do tada ću, nadam se, prestati objašnjavati tu odluku svakoj osobi koju sretnem.
learner.en: See you. By then, I hope I'll have stopped explaining that decision to every person I meet.

conversations.title: Two students agree on shared space

partner.hr: Kako ti se sviđa naš novi studentski stan?
partner.en: How do you like our new student flat?

learner.hr: Sviđa mi se, ali mislim da trebamo dogovor o čišćenju prije nego što nastane nered.
learner.en: I like it, but I think we need an agreement about cleaning before it gets messy.

partner.hr: Hoćemo li napraviti raspored po tjednima?
partner.en: Shall we make a weekly rota?

learner.hr: Možemo. Ja ću ovaj tjedan očistiti kuhinju, a ti kupaonicu, pa ćemo se poslije zamijeniti.
learner.en: Yes. I'll clean the kitchen this week and you can do the bathroom, then we'll swap.

partner.hr: Treba li dogovor i o gostima?
partner.en: Do we need an agreement about guests too?

learner.hr: Treba. Nemam ništa protiv društva, ali želim znati ako će netko prespavati u dnevnoj sobi.
learner.en: Yes. I don't mind having people over, but I'd like to know if someone's going to sleep in the living room.

partner.en: And during exam time?

learner.hr: Tada mi treba više tišine. Na sveučilištu nemamo uvijek slobodnu učionicu za učenje.
learner.en: I'll need more quiet then. We don't always have a free classroom for studying at the university.

partner.en: I prefer studying early in the morning.

learner.hr: A ja radije učim navečer. Možemo koristiti slušalice i zatvarati vrata da ne ometamo jedno drugo.
learner.en: I prefer studying in the evening. We can use headphones and close the doors so we don't disturb each other.

partner.hr: Izgleda da ćemo se lako dogovoriti.
partner.en: It looks as though we'll agree easily.

learner.hr: Nadam se. Bolje je jasno reći što nam treba nego mjesecima skupljati ljutnju zbog prljave šalice.
learner.en: I hope so. It's better to say clearly what we need than build up months of resentment over a dirty cup.

conversations.title: Giving an old coat a second life

partner.hr: Zašto nosiš taj stari kaput krojačici?
partner.en: Why are you taking that old coat to the tailor?

learner.hr: Zato što mi je još drag. Podstava je poderana, ali vanjski dio izgleda dobro.
learner.en: Because I'm still fond of it. The lining is torn, but the outside looks good.

partner.en: Wouldn't it be simpler to buy a new one?

learner.hr: Možda jest, ali ne želim baciti nešto što se može popraviti i ponovno nositi.
learner.en: Maybe, but I don't want to throw away something that can be repaired and worn again.

partner.hr: Što bi još promijenila na njemu?
partner.en: What else would you change about it?

learner.hr: Skratila bih rukave i zamijenila gumbe. Ovi metalni su teški i ne sviđa mi se njihov oblik.
learner.en: I'd shorten the sleeves and replace the buttons. These metal ones are heavy, and I don't like their shape.

partner.en: Have you got new buttons already?

learner.hr: Imam nekoliko crnih i smeđih, ali ponijet ću sve da usporedimo boje na dnevnom svjetlu.
learner.en: I've got a few black and brown ones, but I'll take them all so we can compare the colours in daylight.

partner.en: Can you sew yourself?

learner.hr: Znam zašiti manju rupu, ali ovo traži više vještine i bolji stroj nego što ga imam.
learner.en: I can sew up a small hole, but this needs more skill and a better machine than I have.

partner.hr: Pokaži mi rezultat kad bude gotov.
partner.en: Show me the result when it's ready.

learner.hr: Hoću. Ako uspije kako sam zamislila, možda će mi to postati omiljeni kaput umjesto stare uspomene.
learner.en: I will. If it turns out as I've imagined, it may become my favourite coat rather than an old keepsake.

conversations.title: Changing the ending of a bedtime story

partner.hr: Zašto si zatvorila knjigu prije kraja?
partner.en: Why did you close the book before the end?

learner.hr: Ne sviđa mi se što se vještica pretvori u kamen. Želim drukčiji završetak.
learner.en: I don't like the witch turning to stone. I want a different ending.

partner.en: What ending would you write?

learner.hr: Djevojčica bi je prvo pitala zašto je tako ljuta, umjesto da odmah pobjegne od nje.
learner.en: The little girl would first ask why she's so angry rather than run away from her straight away.

partner.hr: A ako je vještica stvarno opasna?
partner.en: What if the witch really is dangerous?

learner.hr: Onda ne bi morala ostati sama s njom. Mogla bi pozvati nekog odraslog da joj pomogne.
learner.en: Then she wouldn't have to stay alone with her. She could call an adult to help.

partner.hr: Misliš da bi vještica pristala razgovarati?
partner.en: Do you think the witch would agree to talk?

learner.hr: Možda ne odmah. Ali mogla bi barem dobiti priliku da prestane raditi zlo.
learner.en: Maybe not at first. But she could at least have a chance to stop doing harm.

partner.hr: Želiš li sutra nacrtati svoj završetak?
partner.en: Would you like to draw your ending tomorrow?

learner.hr: Želim. Nacrtat ću malu kuću, veliku šumu i stol za kojim mogu razgovarati.
learner.en: Yes. I'll draw a small house, a big forest and a table where they can talk.

partner.hr: A sad je vrijeme za spavanje.
partner.en: And now it's time for bed.

learner.hr: Dobro. Samo nemoj ostaviti knjigu otvorenu, da ona stara vještica ne vidi da joj mijenjamo priču.
learner.en: All right. Just don't leave the book open, or that old witch will see we're changing her story.

conversations.title: Three plans on the same weekend

partner.hr: Jesi li vidio koliko obaveza imamo u svibnju?
partner.en: Have you seen how many commitments we have in May?

learner.hr: Jesam. Jednog vikenda imamo vjenčanje, rođendan i roditeljski sastanak u školi.
learner.en: Yes. One weekend we've got a wedding, a birthday and a parents' meeting at school.

partner.hr: Kako ćemo biti na tri mjesta?
partner.en: How will we be in three places?

learner.hr: Ne možemo. Moramo provjeriti točne datume, jer mislim da smo nešto pogrešno upisali.
learner.en: We can't. We need to check the exact dates because I think we wrote something down incorrectly.

partner.en: The wedding is on the fifteenth of May.

learner.hr: A rođendan je petnaestog lipnja. Eto, jedna obaveza već je nestala iz tog vikenda.
learner.en: And the birthday is on the fifteenth of June. There, one commitment has already disappeared from that weekend.

partner.hr: Sastanak u školi ipak je u petak.
partner.en: The school meeting is actually on Friday.

learner.hr: Onda možemo ići na oboje, samo ne smijemo planirati putovanje prije petka navečer.
learner.en: Then we can go to both; we just mustn't plan to travel before Friday evening.

partner.hr: Dobro je da smo sve provjerili.
partner.en: It's a good thing we checked everything.

learner.hr: Jest. Inače bismo prijateljima čestitali mjesec dana prerano i još im objasnili da nemamo vremena za njih.
learner.en: Yes. Otherwise we'd have wished our friends a happy birthday a month early and told them we had no time for them.

partner.en: Will you update the calendar now?

learner.hr: Hoću. Ovaj put ću provjeriti i godinu, da nas ne iznenadi nešto što je već prošlo.
learner.en: Yes. This time I'll check the year too, so we aren't surprised by something that's already happened.

conversations.title: Learning to dance without pretending

partner.hr: Zašto stojiš iza svih u plesnoj dvorani?
partner.en: Why are you standing behind everyone in the dance hall?

learner.hr: Zato što stalno krenem pogrešnom nogom i onda se sudarim s osobom pored sebe.
learner.en: Because I keep starting with the wrong foot and then bumping into the person beside me.

partner.en: We're all beginners here.

learner.hr: Znam, ali neki barem mogu razlikovati lijevu od desne kad počne glazba.
learner.en: I know, but some people can at least tell left from right when the music starts.

partner.hr: Hoćeš li probati polako sa mnom?
partner.en: Would you like to try slowly with me?

learner.hr: Hoću. Samo mi prvo pokaži pokret bez glazbe, da ne pokušavam pratiti sve odjednom.
learner.en: Yes. Just show me the movement without music first so I'm not trying to follow everything at once.

partner.hr: Ovako, dva koraka naprijed pa jedan u stranu.
partner.en: Like this: two steps forward, then one to the side.

learner.hr: A-ha, sad vidim. Težinu trebam prebaciti na drugu nogu prije okreta.
learner.en: Aha, now I see. I need to shift my weight onto the other foot before turning.

partner.en: That's right. See, you can do it.

learner.hr: Mogu dok ne počnem previše razmišljati. Tijelo mi je sporije od želje da odmah budem dobar.
learner.en: I can until I start overthinking. My body is slower than my wish to be good straight away.

partner.en: We've got the whole course to practise.

learner.hr: Dobro. Onda ću prestati stajati kao stup i barem pokušati uživati.
learner.en: Good. Then I'll stop standing around like a post and at least try to enjoy it.

conversations.title: Watching a storm from indoors

partner.hr: Jesi li zatvorio prozore na katu?
partner.en: Have you closed the upstairs windows?

learner.hr: Jesam. Vjetar je odjednom postao jak i kiša je počela ulaziti u hodnik.
learner.en: Yes. The wind suddenly got strong, and rain started coming into the hall.

partner.hr: Što je s rubljem na balkonu?
partner.en: What about the washing on the balcony?

learner.hr: Unio sam ga na vrijeme. Još je malo vlažno, ali barem nije završilo u susjedovu vrtu.
learner.en: I brought it in in time. It's still a little damp, but at least it didn't end up in the neighbour's garden.

partner.en: Can you hear the thunder?

learner.hr: Čujem. Naš mačak već se sakrio ispod kreveta i ne želi izaći.
learner.en: Yes. Our cat has already hidden under the bed and won't come out.

partner.en: Will you bring him his blanket?

learner.hr: Hoću, ali neću ga tjerati da se pomakne. Čini se da mu je ondje mirnije.
learner.en: Yes, but I won't force him to move. He seems calmer there.

partner.hr: Dobro je da smo otkazali šetnju.
partner.en: It's a good thing we cancelled our walk.

learner.hr: Jest. Sada mi je draže sjediti u toploj sobi i gledati kako se nebo mijenja kroz staklo.
learner.en: Yes. Right now I'd rather sit in a warm room and watch the sky change through the glass.

partner.hr: Napravit ću kakao dok ne prođe.
partner.en: I'll make cocoa while we wait for it to pass.

learner.hr: Odlično. A poslije ćemo provjeriti je li u vrtu sve ostalo na svom mjestu.
learner.en: Great. Afterwards we'll check that everything in the garden is still in place.

conversations.title: Old coins and a child who likes numbers

partner.hr: Zašto gledaš baš te male predmete?
partner.en: Why are you looking at those little objects in particular?

learner.hr: To su stari novčići. Na svakome je drukčije lice i broj koji ne znam pročitati.
learner.en: They're old coins. Each one has a different face and a number I can't read.

partner.hr: Možda su brojevi zapisani na drugi način.
partner.en: Maybe the numbers are written differently.

learner.hr: Možda. Ovdje piše da su neki novčići stariji od tisuću godina.
learner.en: Maybe. It says here that some of the coins are more than a thousand years old.

partner.hr: Što bi ih htio pitati kad bi mogli govoriti?
partner.en: What would you like to ask them if they could talk?

learner.hr: Koliko su ruku promijenili i što su ljudi za njih nekad mogli kupiti.
learner.en: How many hands they've passed through and what people could once buy with them.

partner.hr: Bi li radije imao jedan takav ili novu igračku?
partner.en: Would you rather have one of those or a new toy?

learner.hr: Za igranje igračku, ali za priču novčić. Ne mora sve vrijediti samo zbog cijene.
learner.en: A toy for playing, but a coin for its story. Not everything has to matter only because of its price.

partner.en: That's a lovely thought.

learner.hr: Mislim da ću nacrtati vlastiti novac kad dođemo kući, s našim psom umjesto kralja.
learner.en: I think I'll draw my own money when we get home, with our dog instead of a king.

partner.en: How much will it be worth?

learner.hr: Jedan novčić za jednu pseću poslasticu. To je valuta koju bi on sigurno razumio.
learner.en: One coin for one dog treat. That's a currency he'd certainly understand.

conversations.title: A handwritten note in a borrowed book

partner.hr: Jesi li u knjizi pronašla papirić?
partner.en: Did you find the little piece of paper in the book?

learner.hr: Jesam. Bio je između zadnjih stranica, baš gdje sam sinoć prestala čitati.
learner.en: Yes. It was between the last few pages, right where I stopped reading last night.

partner.hr: Nisam bila sigurna hoćeš li ga primijetiti.
partner.en: I wasn't sure whether you'd notice it.

learner.hr: Primijetila sam ga i nasmijala se. Nisam očekivala poruku o našem prvom susretu.
learner.en: I noticed it and smiled. I wasn't expecting a note about the first time we met.

partner.hr: Sjećaš li se onog izgubljenog kišobrana?
partner.en: Do you remember that lost umbrella?

learner.hr: Kako ne bih? Obje smo tvrdile da je naš, a na kraju je pripadao trećoj djevojci.
learner.en: How could I forget? We both insisted it was ours, and in the end it belonged to a third girl.

partner.hr: Ona je morala misliti da smo lude.
partner.en: She must have thought we were crazy.

learner.hr: Vjerojatno. Ali zahvaljujući toj zabuni nas dvije smo otišle na kavu i postale prijateljice.
learner.en: Probably. But thanks to that mix-up, the two of us went for coffee and became friends.

partner.en: Will you keep the note?

learner.hr: Hoću. Stavit ću je u svoju omiljenu knjigu, da je opet pronađem kad je najmanje očekujem.
learner.en: Yes. I'll put it in my favourite book so I can find it again when I least expect it.

partner.en: Then it has served its purpose.

learner.hr: Jest. Ponekad običan komad papira kaže više nego stotinu brzih poruka na telefonu.
learner.en: Yes. Sometimes an ordinary piece of paper says more than a hundred quick messages on a phone.

conversations.title: Arriving in an unfamiliar city

partner.en: Hello, are you looking for the exit?

learner.hr: Dobar dan. Da, prvi put sam na ovom kolodvoru i nemam pojma kamo trebam ići.
learner.en: Hello. Yes, this is my first time at this station, and I have no idea which way to go.

partner.hr: Idete li prema centru ili autobusnoj stanici?
partner.en: Are you heading towards the centre or the bus stop?

learner.hr: Prema centru. Moj prijatelj čeka me ispred glavnog ulaza, ali ne vidim nijedan znak.
learner.en: Towards the centre. My friend is waiting outside the main entrance, but I can't see any signs.

partner.hr: Pođite ovim hodnikom pa skrenite desno.
partner.en: Go down this corridor, then turn right.

learner.hr: Hvala. Moram li silaziti stepenicama ili postoji dizalo? Ovaj kovčeg prilično je težak.
learner.en: Thank you. Do I need to go down stairs, or is there a lift? This suitcase is quite heavy.

partner.hr: Dizalo je pored kioska, iza onog stupa.
partner.en: The lift is beside the kiosk, behind that pillar.

learner.hr: Sad ga vidim. Zaboravio sam koliko putovanje može biti naporno kad ne poznaješ mjesto.
learner.en: I can see it now. I'd forgotten how tiring travelling can be when you don't know a place.

partner.en: Where have you come from?

learner.hr: Iz malog mjesta u kojem svi znaju svaku ulicu. Ovdje mi se čini da svi hodaju brže od mene.
learner.en: A small town where everyone knows every street. Here it feels as though everyone walks faster than I do.

partner.en: You'll get used to it. Enjoy your stay.

learner.hr: Hvala vam na ljubaznosti. Zbog ovakve pomoći i velik grad odmah djeluje manje stran.
learner.en: Thank you for your kindness. Help like this makes even a big city feel less unfamiliar straight away.

conversations.title: Noticing a friend has changed her hair

partner.en: Hey, do you recognise me at all?

learner.hr: Hej! Izgledaš drukčije. Jesi li skratila kosu ili mi se samo čini?
learner.en: Hey! You look different. Have you cut your hair short, or does it just seem that way?

partner.hr: Skratila sam je puno više nego što sam planirala.
partner.en: I've cut it much shorter than I'd planned.

learner.hr: Lijepo ti stoji. Čini mi se da ti se sad lice bolje vidi, pogotovo oči.
learner.en: It suits you. I think your face is more visible now, especially your eyes.

partner.hr: Stvarno to misliš ili me samo tješiš?
partner.en: Do you really think so, or are you just trying to make me feel better?

learner.hr: Stvarno mislim. Ali važnije je sviđa li se tebi nego što ja kažem.
learner.en: I really think so. But whether you like it matters more than what I say.

partner.hr: Još se navikavam kad pogledam u ogledalo.
partner.en: I'm still getting used to it when I look in the mirror.

learner.hr: Razumijem. Kad sam ja promijenila boju kose, nekoliko dana nisam znala što mislim o tome.
learner.en: I understand. When I changed my hair colour, I didn't know how I felt about it for a few days.

partner.hr: Sad barem ne trošim pola jutra na sušenje.
partner.en: At least I don't spend half the morning drying it now.

learner.hr: Onda već imaš jednu veliku prednost. Možeš duže spavati, a i dalje stići na posao.
learner.en: Then you've already got one big advantage. You can sleep longer and still get to work on time.

partner.hr: To mi je zapravo najbolji dio promjene.
partner.en: That's actually the best part of the change.

learner.hr: Vjerujem ti. Hoćemo li sad na kavu prije nego što počnem i sama razmišljati o škarama?
learner.en: I believe you. Shall we get coffee before I start thinking about scissors myself?

conversations.title: A parent after a graduation ceremony

partner.hr: Zašto si tako tih nakon dodjele diploma?
partner.en: Why are you so quiet after the graduation ceremony?

learner.hr: Pokušavam shvatiti da je moj sin završio fakultet. Još ga pamtim kao dječaka s prevelikom školskom torbom.
learner.en: I'm trying to take in the fact that my son has graduated. I still remember him as a boy with a schoolbag that was too big for him.

partner.en: You must be proud of him.

learner.hr: Jesam, jako. Ali nisam ponosan samo zbog diplome, nego i zato što nije odustao kad mu je bilo teško.
learner.en: I am, very. But I'm not proud only because of the degree, but also because he didn't give up when things were hard.

partner.en: Will you tell him that?

learner.hr: Hoću. Ponekad mislim da on već zna kako se osjećam, pa zaboravim izgovoriti ono bitno.
learner.en: Yes. Sometimes I think he already knows how I feel, and I forget to say what matters.

partner.hr: Sad je dobar trenutak. Eno ga s prijateljima.
partner.en: Now is a good moment. There he is with his friends.

learner.hr: Vidim. Sačekat ću da završe fotografiranje pa ću mu prići bez velikog govora.
learner.en: I see him. I'll wait until they've finished taking photos, then go over without making a big speech.

partner.en: Have you bought him a gift?

learner.hr: Jesam, sat. Na poleđini sam dao ugravirati datum i nekoliko riječi za budućnost.
learner.en: Yes, a watch. I had the date and a few words for the future engraved on the back.

partner.hr: Mislim da će mu to puno značiti.
partner.en: I think that will mean a lot to him.

learner.hr: Nadam se. Želim da zna da sam uz njega, bez obzira na to kakav će posao jednog dana raditi.
learner.en: I hope so. I want him to know I'm there for him, whatever work he ends up doing one day.

conversations.title: Admitting dinner has gone wrong

partner.hr: Jesam li došao prerano na večeru?
partner.en: Have I arrived too early for dinner?

learner.hr: Nisi, ja sam počela prekasno. Moram priznati da još ništa nije gotovo.
learner.en: No, I started too late. I have to admit nothing's ready yet.

partner.en: Can I help?

learner.hr: Možeš oprati salatu. Ja ću pokušati spasiti umak prije nego što se potpuno zalijepi za dno.
learner.en: You can wash the lettuce. I'll try to save the sauce before it sticks completely to the bottom.

partner.en: What happened?

learner.hr: Odgovarala sam na poruku i izgubila pojam o vremenu. Sad znam da ne mogu raditi pet stvari odjednom.
learner.en: I was replying to a message and lost track of time. Now I know I can't do five things at once.

partner.en: The sauce smells a little smoky.

learner.hr: Znam. Dovraga, baš sam htjela da sve bude posebno jer se dugo nismo vidjeli.
learner.en: I know. Damn, I really wanted everything to be special because we haven't seen each other for so long.

partner.hr: Meni je posebno već to što večeramo zajedno.
partner.en: Just having dinner together is special to me.

learner.hr: Hvala ti. Onda ću prestati glumiti da je ovo planirani okus i napraviti jednostavniju večeru.
learner.en: Thank you. Then I'll stop pretending this is how it's meant to taste and make a simpler dinner.

partner.hr: Možemo naručiti nešto ako ti je lakše.
partner.en: We can order something if that's easier for you.

learner.hr: Možemo. A tajni recept za spaljeni umak zadržat ću za sebe, da ga slučajno netko ne ponovi.
learner.en: Let's do that. And I'll keep my secret burnt-sauce recipe to myself so nobody accidentally repeats it.

conversations.title: Remembering an old family dog

partner.hr: Je li ti čudno doći kući bez psa na vratima?
partner.en: Does it feel strange to come home without the dog at the door?

learner.hr: Jest. Godinama me dočekivao na istom mjestu, pa mi je tišina sad nekako prevelika.
learner.en: Yes. He greeted me in the same place for years, so the silence feels too big now.

partner.en: Would you like to talk about him?

learner.hr: Želim. Svi pokušavaju promijeniti temu, ali meni je drago prisjetiti se koliko je bio smiješan.
learner.en: Yes. Everyone tries to change the subject, but I like remembering how funny he was.

partner.hr: Sjećam se da je jednom ukrao cijeli kruh.
partner.en: I remember him stealing a whole loaf once.

learner.hr: I onda ga je sakrio u moj krevet. Pravio se da nema nikakve veze s tim, a mrvice su mu bile na nosu.
learner.en: And then he hid it in my bed. He pretended he had nothing to do with it, but there were crumbs on his nose.

partner.hr: Takav je bio od prvog dana.
partner.en: That's what he was like from the first day.

learner.hr: Jest. Njegova smrt bila mi je teška, ali ne želim da to izbriše sve lijepe godine prije nje.
learner.en: Yes. His death was hard for me, but I don't want that to erase all the lovely years before it.

partner.hr: Imaš li još njegovu staru ogrlicu?
partner.en: Have you still got his old collar?

learner.hr: Imam. Stavit ću je uz fotografiju iz vrta, na kojoj je još mlad i pun energije.
learner.en: Yes. I'll put it beside the garden photograph where he's still young and full of energy.

partner.hr: Mogu ti pomoći izabrati sliku ako želiš.
partner.en: I can help you choose a picture if you like.

learner.hr: Hvala. To bi mi značilo više nego savjet da jednostavno nabavim drugog psa.
learner.en: Thank you. That would mean more to me than advice to simply get another dog.

conversations.title: A captain in a board game

partner.hr: Tko će biti kapetan u ovoj igri?
partner.en: Who's going to be the captain in this game?

learner.hr: Ja ću, ako se ostali slažu. Samo mi prvo objasnite što moram učiniti u prvom krugu.
learner.en: I will, if everyone agrees. Just explain what I have to do in the first round first.

partner.hr: Moraš odabrati smjer plovidbe i podijeliti zalihe.
partner.en: You have to choose the sailing direction and distribute supplies.

learner.hr: Dobro. Onda ne idemo ravno u oluju, koliko god blago na karti izgledalo privlačno.
learner.en: All right. Then we're not sailing straight into the storm, however tempting the treasure on the map looks.

partner.hr: Ali tako bi mogli pobijediti prije ostalih.
partner.en: But that way we could win before everyone else.

learner.hr: Mogli bismo, ali mogli bismo i izgubiti brod. Radije bih prvo saznao kako djeluju pravila.
learner.en: We could, but we could also lose the ship. I'd rather first find out how the rules work.

partner.en: Captain, the crew wants a quicker decision.

learner.hr: Posada će dobiti odluku čim prestane prekidati kapetana dok čita upute.
learner.en: The crew will get a decision as soon as it stops interrupting the captain while he's reading the instructions.

partner.hr: Dobro, zasad ćemo čekati u luci.
partner.en: All right, we'll wait in port for now.

learner.hr: Odlično. Dajte mi kartu i jednu minutu mira, pa ćemo možda i preživjeti do drugog kruga.
learner.en: Great. Give me the map and a minute's peace, and we might even survive until the second round.

partner.hr: Mislim da će ovo biti duga večer.
partner.en: I think this is going to be a long evening.

learner.hr: Hoće, ali obećavam da ću vas dovesti do otoka prije nego što nestane svih grickalica.
learner.en: It will, but I promise I'll get you to the island before all the snacks disappear.

conversations.title: Two group bookings with the same surname

partner.hr: Dobra večer, vi ste grupa na ime Kovač?
partner.en: Good evening, are you the group booked under Kovač?

learner.hr: Jesmo, ali naša rezervacija je za šest osoba. Ovdje vidim postavljen stol za dvanaest.
learner.en: Yes, but our booking is for six people. I can see a table set for twelve here.

partner.en: I may have mixed up two bookings.

learner.hr: Moguće. Zovem se Ana Kovač, a rezervirala sam u ponedjeljak za današnjih osam sati.
learner.en: Possibly. My name is Ana Kovač, and I booked on Monday for eight o'clock today.

partner.hr: Da, našao sam vašu. Manji stol je uz prozor.
partner.en: Yes, I've found yours. The smaller table is by the window.

learner.hr: Hvala. Gospođo, možete li vi prva sjesti? Ostavit ćemo vam mjesto s više prostora za noge.
learner.en: Thank you. Madam, would you like to sit down first? We'll leave you the seat with more legroom.

partner.en: Do you need a children's menu?

learner.hr: Ne treba, svi smo odrasli. Samo vas molim da jelovnik donesete i gospodinu koji još skida kaput.
learner.en: No, we're all adults. Just please bring a menu for the gentleman who's still taking off his coat too.

partner.en: Would you like to order straight away?

learner.hr: Još ne. Pričekat ćemo našu prijateljicu, pa možete uzeti sva jela zajedno.
learner.en: Not yet. We'll wait for our friend, then you can take all the food orders together.

partner.hr: U redu, javite mi kad budete spremni.
partner.en: All right, let me know when you're ready.

learner.hr: Hoćemo, hvala. Drago mi je da smo razjasnili rezervaciju prije nego što smo zauzeli tuđu polovicu restorana.
learner.en: We will, thank you. I'm glad we cleared up the booking before taking over someone else's half of the restaurant.

conversations.title: A birthday photograph with twins

partner.hr: Možeš li razlikovati blizance na ovoj fotografiji?
partner.en: Can you tell the twins apart in this photograph?

learner.hr: Mogu. Luka je onaj koji drži tortu, a njegov brat sjedi pored naše sestre.
learner.en: Yes. Luka's the one holding the cake, and his brother is sitting beside our sister.

partner.en: They look exactly the same to me.

learner.hr: Izgledaju slično, ali imaju drukčiji osmijeh. Osim toga, Luka nikad ne nosi košulju s gumbima.
learner.en: They look similar, but they smile differently. Besides, Luka never wears a shirt with buttons.

partner.hr: A tko je djevojka iza njih?
partner.en: And who's the girl behind them?

learner.hr: To je prijateljica njihove majke. Došla je iz drugog grada samo zbog rođendana.
learner.en: That's their mother's friend. She came from another city just for the birthday.

partner.hr: Izgleda kao da svi gledaju na drugu stranu.
partner.en: It looks as though everyone's looking in the other direction.

learner.hr: Da, jer je netko baš tada ispustio balon. Djeca su ga pratila pogledom umjesto da gledaju u kameru.
learner.en: Yes, because someone let go of a balloon just then. The children followed it with their eyes instead of looking at the camera.

partner.en: It's still a lovely memory.

learner.hr: Meni je najbolja od svih slika. Nije savršena, ali pokazuje kakva je zabava stvarno bila.
learner.en: To me it's the best of all the pictures. It isn't perfect, but it shows what the party was really like.

partner.hr: Hoćeš li je ispisati za album?
partner.en: Will you print it for the album?

learner.hr: Hoću. I napisat ću imena na poleđini, da za dvadeset godina opet ne raspravljamo tko je tko.
learner.en: Yes. And I'll write the names on the back so we aren't arguing about who's who again in twenty years.

conversations.title: A friend appears in a holiday video

partner.hr: Jesi li vidio video koji sam objavio s izleta?
partner.en: Have you seen the video I posted from the trip?

learner.hr: Jesam. Snimke su lijepe, ali nisam znao da će se tako jasno vidjeti moje lice.
learner.en: Yes. The footage is lovely, but I didn't know my face would be so clearly visible.

partner.hr: Smeta li ti što si u njemu?
partner.en: Does it bother you to be in it?

learner.hr: Smeta mi taj dio u kojem pričam o svojoj obitelji. Nisam očekivao da će razgovor biti javan.
learner.en: I'm uncomfortable with the part where I'm talking about my family. I didn't expect that conversation to be public.

partner.hr: Oprosti, mislio sam da ti neće smetati.
partner.en: Sorry, I thought you wouldn't mind.

learner.hr: Razumijem, ali radije bih da me sljedeći put pitaš prije objave. Neke stvari želim zadržati za sebe.
learner.en: I understand, but I'd prefer you to ask me before posting next time. I want to keep some things to myself.

partner.en: I can remove that part right away.

learner.hr: Hvala ti. Ostale snimke mogu ostati, samo provjeri čuje li se još negdje naš razgovor.
learner.en: Thank you. The rest of the footage can stay; just check whether our conversation can be heard anywhere else.

partner.hr: Hoćeš li pogledati novu verziju prije nego što je vratim?
partner.en: Would you like to see the new version before I put it back up?

learner.hr: Hoću. To bi mi dalo više povjerenja nego da samo pretpostavimo da je sve u redu.
learner.en: Yes. That would give me more confidence than simply assuming everything's all right.

partner.hr: Dogovoreno, poslat ću ti je večeras.
partner.en: Agreed; I'll send it to you tonight.

learner.hr: Super. Ne želim pokvariti tvoje veselje zbog snimanja, samo jasno reći gdje su moje granice.
learner.en: Great. I don't want to spoil your enjoyment of filming, just make my boundaries clear.

conversations.title: A confusing subtitle in a film

partner.en: Why have you paused the film?

learner.hr: Ovaj prijevod nema smisla. Lik govori o ribi, a ispod piše nešto o banci.
learner.en: This translation doesn't make sense. The character's talking about a fish, but the subtitle says something about a bank.

partner.hr: Možda riječ u izvorniku ima više značenja.
partner.en: Maybe the original word has more than one meaning.

learner.hr: Vjerojatno. Prevoditelj je možda vidio samo tekst, bez prizora koji pokazuje gdje se nalaze.
learner.en: Probably. The translator may have seen only the text, without the scene showing where they are.

partner.en: Can we switch to another translation?

learner.hr: Možemo pokušati. Ovaj ima i nekoliko rečenica koje zvuče kao da ih nitko ne bi stvarno rekao.
learner.en: We can try. This one also has a few sentences that sound as though nobody would actually say them.

partner.hr: Jesi li ti ikad prevodila titlove?
partner.en: Have you ever translated subtitles?

learner.hr: Nisam, ali sam prevodila kratke priče. Znam da nije dovoljno samo zamijeniti jednu riječ drugom.
learner.en: No, but I've translated short stories. I know simply replacing one word with another isn't enough.

partner.en: What did you find hardest?

learner.hr: Zadržati isti ton. Šala može biti točna po riječima, a ipak izgubiti sav humor u prijevodu.
learner.en: Keeping the same tone. A joke can be accurate word for word and still lose all its humour in translation.

partner.en: Shall we carry on watching?

learner.hr: Hoćemo. Ako se pojavi još koja neobična rečenica, barem ćemo imati dodatni razlog za smijeh.
learner.en: Yes. If another odd sentence comes up, at least we'll have an extra reason to laugh.

conversations.title: Checking a rumour before judging a friend

partner.hr: Zašto danas ne razgovaraš s Matijom?
partner.en: Why aren't you speaking to Matija today?

learner.hr: Čuo sam da je drugima rekao nešto ružno o meni. Ne znam mogu li mu vjerovati.
learner.en: I heard he'd said something nasty about me to other people. I don't know if I can trust him.

partner.hr: Jesi li ga pitao što se dogodilo?
partner.en: Have you asked him what happened?

learner.hr: Nisam. Bio sam ljut i nisam htio slušati nikakve izgovore.
learner.en: No. I was angry and didn't want to listen to any excuses.

partner.hr: A tko ti je to uopće rekao?
partner.en: Who actually told you?

learner.hr: Jedan dečko iz drugog razreda. Sad kad pitaš, ni on nije čuo razgovor nego mu je netko prenio.
learner.en: A boy from another class. Now that you ask, he didn't hear the conversation either; someone passed it on to him.

partner.hr: Onda bi priča mogla biti pogrešna.
partner.en: Then the story could be wrong.

learner.hr: Mogla bi. Nije pošteno da prijatelja smatram krivim prije nego što ga išta pitam.
learner.en: It could. It isn't fair to treat my friend as guilty before I've even asked him anything.

partner.hr: Hoćeš li razgovarati s njim nakon nastave?
partner.en: Will you talk to him after class?

learner.hr: Hoću. Reći ću što sam čuo i pitati je li istina, bez napadanja.
learner.en: Yes. I'll say what I heard and ask whether it's true, without attacking him.

partner.hr: Možda se pokaže da je sve nesporazum.
partner.en: Maybe it'll turn out to be a misunderstanding.

learner.hr: Nadam se. A ako sam ga povrijedio šutnjom, morat ću i ja priznati svoj dio pogreške.
learner.en: I hope so. And if I've hurt him by refusing to speak, I'll have to acknowledge my part in the mistake too.

conversations.title: A child after losing a football match

partner.hr: Zašto si bacio dres na pod?
partner.en: Why did you throw your shirt on the floor?

learner.hr: Zato što smo izgubili, a drugi dečki ponašali su se kao da je sve moja krivnja.
learner.en: Because we lost, and the other boys acted as if it were all my fault.

partner.hr: Jesu li to rekli ili si tako zaključio?
partner.en: Did they say that, or is that what you concluded?

learner.hr: Jedan je rekao da sam trebao dodati loptu. Ostali nisu ništa govorili.
learner.en: One said I should have passed the ball. The others didn't say anything.

partner.hr: Što ti misliš o toj situaciji?
partner.en: What do you think about that situation?

learner.hr: Mogao sam dodati, ali imao sam priliku pucati. Da sam zabio, vjerojatno se nitko ne bi žalio.
learner.en: I could have passed, but I had a chance to shoot. If I'd scored, probably nobody would have complained.

partner.hr: Hoćeš li o tome pitati trenera?
partner.en: Will you ask the coach about it?

learner.hr: Hoću, kad se smirim. Sad bih samo rekao da mrzim nogomet, a znam da to nije istina.
learner.en: Yes, once I calm down. Right now I'd just say I hate football, and I know that isn't true.

partner.hr: Što bi ti pomoglo da se smiriš?
partner.en: What would help you calm down?

learner.hr: Malo šetnje bez razgovora o rezultatu. Ne moram odmah pronaći lekciju u svakom porazu.
learner.en: A short walk without talking about the score. I don't have to find a lesson in every defeat straight away.

partner.en: All right, let's go for a walk.

learner.hr: Hvala, tata. A dres ću poslije pokupiti sam, nisam ga trebao tako baciti.
learner.en: Thanks, Dad. And I'll pick up the shirt myself afterwards; I shouldn't have thrown it like that.

conversations.title: A cycling trip takes the wrong turn

partner.hr: Zašto smo opet ispred iste crkve?
partner.en: Why are we in front of the same church again?

learner.hr: Zato što sam, očito, odabrao pogrešan put. Napravili smo cijeli krug umjesto da prijeđemo most.
learner.en: Because I clearly chose the wrong route. We've gone all the way around instead of crossing the bridge.

partner.hr: Zar nisi pogledao kartu prije skretanja?
partner.en: Didn't you look at the map before turning?

learner.hr: Jesam, ali držao sam je okrenutu naopako. Možeš se smijati, zaslužio sam.
learner.en: Yes, but I was holding it upside down. You can laugh; I've earned it.

partner.hr: Neću se smijati ako sada pronađeš pravi smjer.
partner.en: I won't laugh if you find the right direction now.

learner.hr: Onda prvo stani, da ponovno ne krenemo dok nagađam. Most bi trebao biti iza ovog reda kuća.
learner.en: Then stop first so we don't set off again while I'm guessing. The bridge should be behind this row of houses.

partner.en: I can see a sign for the cycle path.

learner.hr: Odlično. To je put koji smo tražili. Sad ćemo voziti uz rijeku, a ne oko središta grada.
learner.en: Great. That's the route we were looking for. Now we'll ride along the river instead of around the city centre.

partner.hr: Hoćemo li još stići prije mraka?
partner.en: Will we still get there before dark?

learner.hr: Hoćemo ako ne stanemo kod svake pekarnice. Ali predlažem da vodstvo ovaj put preuzmeš ti.
learner.en: Yes, if we don't stop at every bakery. But I suggest you take the lead this time.

partner.en: Agreed. Just follow me.

learner.hr: Pratim. Ako se opet izgubimo, barem ćemo imati više različitih ljudi kojima možemo pripisati zasluge.
learner.en: I will. If we get lost again, at least we'll have more than one person to give the credit to.

conversations.title: Declining a street interview politely

partner.hr: Dobar dan, imate li minutu za našu emisiju?
partner.en: Hello, do you have a minute for our programme?

learner.hr: Dobar dan. O čemu je riječ i snimate li već ovaj razgovor?
learner.en: Hello. What is it about, and are you already recording this conversation?

partner.hr: Pitamo prolaznike što misle o gradskom prijevozu. Kamera je uključena.
partner.en: We're asking people what they think about public transport. The camera is on.

learner.hr: Hvala na objašnjenju, ali ne želim da moja izjava bude objavljena.
learner.en: Thank you for explaining, but I don't want my comments published.

partner.en: We don't have to give your name.

learner.hr: Razumijem, ali svejedno ne želim sudjelovati. Radije bih ostala izvan kadra.
learner.en: I understand, but I still don't want to take part. I'd rather stay out of shot.

partner.hr: U redu, nećemo koristiti ovaj dio.
partner.en: All right, we won't use this part.

learner.hr: Hvala vam. Moja prijateljica možda želi razgovarati, ali morate pitati nju osobno.
learner.en: Thank you. My friend might want to talk, but you'll need to ask her personally.

partner.hr: Svakako. Oprostite što smo vas zaustavili.
partner.en: Certainly. Sorry for stopping you.

learner.hr: Nema problema. Samo mi je važno znati gdje će završiti ono što govorim.
learner.en: No problem. It's just important to me to know where what I say will end up.

partner.en: Thank you for your time.

learner.hr: Nema na čemu. Sretno s emisijom i ugodan ostatak dana.
learner.en: You're welcome. Good luck with the programme, and enjoy the rest of your day.

conversations.title: Asking about a difficult family memory

partner.hr: Zašto te zanima baš ta stara fotografija?
partner.en: Why are you interested in that particular old photograph?

learner.hr: U školi govorimo o ratu, a znam da si ti tada bila dijete. Smijem li te nešto pitati?
learner.en: We're talking about the war at school, and I know you were a child then. May I ask you something?

partner.hr: Smiješ, ali možda neću na sve htjeti odgovoriti.
partner.en: You may, but I might not want to answer everything.

learner.hr: Razumijem. Ne trebaš pričati o nečemu što te boli samo zato što sam ja znatiželjna.
learner.en: I understand. You don't need to talk about something painful just because I'm curious.

partner.en: What would you like to know?

learner.hr: Kako ste provodili obične dane. U knjizi piše o bitkama, ali ne i o tome kako su djeca živjela.
learner.en: How you spent ordinary days. The book talks about battles, but not about how children lived.

partner.hr: Igrali smo se kad god smo mogli. To nam je pomagalo.
partner.en: We played whenever we could. It helped us.

learner.hr: To nisam očekivala. Mislila sam da tijekom rata nije bilo mjesta ni za kakvu igru.
learner.en: I hadn't expected that. I thought there wasn't room for any kind of play during a war.

partner.hr: Bilo je straha, ali i ljudi koji su brinuli jedni o drugima.
partner.en: There was fear, but also people who looked after each other.

learner.hr: Željela bih to zapamtiti. Ne želim svesti tvoj život na jednu tužnu rečenicu u svom sastavku.
learner.en: I'd like to remember that. I don't want to reduce your life to one sad sentence in my essay.

partner.hr: Možemo drugi put pogledati ostatak albuma.
partner.en: We can look through the rest of the album another time.

learner.hr: Voljela bih. I pokazat ću ti što napišem prije nego što to podijelim s razredom.
learner.en: I'd like that. And I'll show you what I write before I share it with the class.

conversations.title: A reluctant king in a school play
