partner.hr: Kako je bilo igrati kralja na probi?
partner.en: What was it like playing the king in rehearsal?

learner.hr: Zabavno, dok nisam morao izgovoriti cijeli govor s krunom koja mi pada preko očiju.
learner.en: Fun, until I had to deliver the whole speech with a crown falling over my eyes.

partner.hr: Što tvoji podanici rade dok govoriš?
partner.en: What do your subjects do while you're speaking?

learner.hr: Jedan me stalno zove gospodaru, a drugi mi se obraća s vaše veličanstvo. Onda se obojica počnu smijati.
learner.en: One keeps calling me master, and the other addresses me as Your Majesty. Then they both start laughing.

partner.en: Maybe that's part of the comedy.

learner.hr: Jest, ali ne kad i ja zaboravim tekst. Kralj koji samo šuti nije baš uvjerljiv.
learner.en: It is, but not when I forget my lines too. A king who just stays silent isn't very convincing.

partner.hr: Možeš li zamoliti da ti poprave krunu?
partner.en: Can you ask them to fix the crown?

learner.hr: Već jesam. Naša učiteljica rekla je da će staviti vrpcu s unutarnje strane.
learner.en: I already have. Our teacher said she'd put a ribbon on the inside.

partner.en: Then all you need to do is learn the speech.

learner.hr: Znam. Najteža mi je rečenica o tome da kralj mora služiti narodu, a ne narod njemu.
learner.en: I know. The hardest line is the one about a king needing to serve the people rather than the people serving him.

partner.en: That sounds like an important message.

learner.hr: Jest. Samo se nadam da će je publika čuti prije nego što kralj počne loviti vlastitu krunu po podu.
learner.en: It is. I just hope the audience hears it before the king starts chasing his own crown across the floor.

conversations.title: A career change after years in one job

partner.hr: Je li istina da napuštaš posao?
partner.en: Is it true you're leaving your job?

learner.hr: Jest. Dao sam otkaz nakon mnogo razmišljanja, ali još nisam siguran što ću dalje.
learner.en: Yes. I handed in my notice after thinking it through a lot, but I'm still not sure what I'll do next.

partner.hr: Što te navelo na tu odluku?
partner.en: What led you to that decision?

learner.hr: Godinama sam čekao da se nešto promijeni, a svaki sam se dan vraćao kući sve umorniji.
learner.en: For years I waited for something to change, and every day I came home more tired.

partner.hr: Imaš li dovoljno vremena potražiti drugi posao?
partner.en: Do you have enough time to look for another job?

learner.hr: Imam nešto ušteđevine, pa ne moram prihvatiti prvu ponudu. Ipak ću pažljivo planirati troškove.
learner.en: I've got some savings, so I don't have to accept the first offer. Still, I'll plan my expenses carefully.

partner.hr: Kakvim bi se poslom želio baviti?
partner.en: What kind of work would you like to do?

learner.hr: Nečim u čemu mogu vidjeti rezultat svog rada. Dosad sam uglavnom slao izvještaje koje nitko nije čitao.
learner.en: Something where I can see the result of my work. Until now I've mostly sent reports that nobody read.

partner.hr: Možda bi ti koristio razgovor s nekim iz drugog područja.
partner.en: Maybe talking to someone from another field would help.

learner.hr: Slažem se. Moj bivši kolega radi u maloj radionici, pa ću ga pitati kako mu izgleda običan dan.
learner.en: I agree. My former colleague works in a small workshop, so I'll ask what an ordinary day is like for him.

partner.hr: Drago mi je da si odlučio pokušati.
partner.en: I'm glad you've decided to give it a try.

learner.hr: I meni, iako me strah. Ne očekujem savršen posao, samo život u kojem imam malo više prostora za sebe.
learner.en: So am I, although I'm scared. I don't expect a perfect job, just a life with a little more room for myself.

conversations.title: Finding a lost wedding ring in the garden

partner.en: Why are you searching the soil around the roses?

learner.hr: Izgubila sam prsten dok sam radila u vrtu. Mislim da mi je skliznuo kad sam skinula rukavice.
learner.en: I lost my ring while working in the garden. I think it slipped off when I took off my gloves.

partner.en: Have you looked inside them?

learner.hr: Jesam, ali u njima nema prstena. Sad se bojim da sam ga zakopala dok sam sadila cvijeće.
learner.en: Yes, but the ring isn't in them. Now I'm afraid I buried it while planting flowers.

partner.en: Can I help you look?

learner.hr: Molim te. Samo nemoj pomaknuti cijelu hrpu zemlje, da ga ne odnesemo još dalje.
learner.en: Please. Just don't move the whole pile of soil, or we might carry it farther away.

partner.hr: Vidiš li nešto sjajno ispod ovog lista?
partner.en: Can you see something shiny under this leaf?

learner.hr: Vidim. Čekaj, to je on! Ne mogu vjerovati da je bio tako blizu mojih nogu.
learner.en: Yes. Wait, that's it! I can't believe it was so close to my feet.

partner.hr: Dobro je da si ga primijetila prije mraka.
partner.en: It's a good thing you noticed it before dark.

learner.hr: Hvala ti. Nije najskuplji prsten na svijetu, ali ne bih ga zamijenila ni za kakvo zlato.
learner.en: Thank you. It isn't the world's most expensive ring, but I wouldn't exchange it for any amount of gold.

partner.en: Will you carry on working today?

learner.hr: Hoću, ali prsten prvo nosim u kuću. Ova mi je mala potraga bila dovoljna pustolovina za jedan dan.
learner.en: Yes, but I'm taking the ring into the house first. This little search was enough adventure for one day.

conversations.title: Joining a chess game in the park

partner.en: Would you like to play a game?

learner.hr: Rado, ali dugo nisam igrao. Trebat će mi malo vremena da ponovno uđem u igru.
learner.en: I'd love to, but I haven't played for a long time. I'll need a little time to get back into it.

partner.hr: Ne žurimo nikamo. Hoćete li bijele figure?
partner.en: We're not in any hurry. Would you like the white pieces?

learner.hr: Hoću, hvala. Tako barem prvi potez mogu pripisati sebi, a ne vašem dobrom početku.
learner.en: Yes, thank you. That way I can at least take credit for the first move rather than your good start.

partner.en: Did you use to play often?

learner.hr: Svakog vikenda sa svojim ocem. On je obožavao smišljati zamke, čak i kad je tvrdio da me samo uči.
learner.en: Every weekend with my father. He loved setting traps, even when he claimed he was only teaching me.

partner.hr: Što bi rekao na ovaj vaš potez?
partner.en: What would he say about that move?

learner.hr: Rekao bi da sam ostavio kraljicu bez zaštite. Sad to vidim i ja, samo malo prekasno.
learner.en: He'd say I've left my queen unprotected. I can see that now too, just a little too late.

partner.hr: Želite li vratiti potez? Ovo nije turnir.
partner.en: Would you like to take the move back? This isn't a tournament.

learner.hr: Hvala, ali neću. Neka mi pogreška ostane u pamćenju do sljedeće partije.
learner.en: Thank you, but I won't. Let the mistake stay in my memory until the next game.

partner.hr: Znači, bit će i sljedeće partije?
partner.en: So there'll be another game?

learner.hr: Bit će, ako me želite ponovno pobijediti. Dugo se nisam ovako dobro zabavio gubeći.
learner.en: Yes, if you'd like to beat me again. I haven't had this much fun losing for a long time.

conversations.title: A family meal in two languages

partner.hr: Zašto za stolom tako malo govoriš?
partner.en: Why are you so quiet at the table?

learner.hr: Pokušavam pratiti razgovor na hrvatskom. Kad svi počnete pričati odjednom, izgubim se.
learner.en: I'm trying to follow the conversation in Croatian. When you all start talking at once, I get lost.

partner.hr: Hoćeš li da prijeđemo na engleski?
partner.en: Would you like us to switch to English?

learner.hr: Ne morate svi. Samo mi katkad objasnite o čemu pričamo, da se mogu ponovno uključiti.
learner.en: Not all of you. Just explain what we're talking about sometimes so I can join in again.

partner.hr: Sad razgovaramo o ljetovanju kod bake.
partner.en: We're talking about staying at Grandma's in the summer.

learner.hr: Aha, onda mogu nešto reći. Sjećam se da smo prošlog ljeta jeli najviše rajčica u životu.
learner.en: Ah, then I can say something. I remember eating more tomatoes last summer than ever before.

partner.hr: Baka će biti sretna da si to zapamtio.
partner.en: Grandma will be happy you remember that.

learner.hr: Jesam, i njen vrt i miris kuhinje. Samo ne znam sve riječi kojima bih to opisao.
learner.en: I do remember her garden and the smell of the kitchen too. I just don't know all the words to describe it.

partner.hr: Možeš opisati i jednostavno. Ne mora biti savršeno.
partner.en: You can describe it simply too. It doesn't need to be perfect.

learner.hr: To mi pomaže čuti. Kad me netko stalno ispravlja, počnem razmišljati više o pogreškama nego o priči.
learner.en: It helps to hear that. When someone keeps correcting me, I start thinking more about mistakes than about the story.

partner.en: Then we'll listen to the story first.

learner.hr: Hvala vam. Ako zapnem, pitam vas za riječ, a ostalo ću pokušati svojim riječima.
learner.en: Thank you. If I get stuck, I'll ask you for the word and try to say the rest in my own words.

conversations.title: Helping guests who arrive before their room is ready

partner.hr: Dobar dan, imamo rezervaciju, ali došli smo prerano.
partner.en: Hello, we have a booking, but we've arrived early.

learner.hr: Dobar dan i dobrodošli. Molim vas, recite mi svoje prezime pa ću provjeriti je li vaša soba spremna.
learner.en: Hello and welcome. Please tell me your surname, and I'll check whether your room is ready.

partner.en: The booking is under Horvat.

learner.hr: Hvala. Vidim vašu rezervaciju, ali soba se još čisti. Možete ostaviti torbe ovdje i otići na ručak.
learner.en: Thank you. I can see your booking, but the room is still being cleaned. You can leave your bags here and go for lunch.

partner.en: Roughly how long will we wait?

learner.hr: Otprilike četrdeset minuta. Ako želite, ostavite broj telefona pa ću vas nazvati čim završimo.
learner.en: About forty minutes. If you like, leave a phone number, and I'll call as soon as we're finished.

partner.hr: Imate li preporuku za ručak u blizini?
partner.en: Can you recommend somewhere nearby for lunch?

learner.hr: Imamo mali restoran u sljedećoj ulici. Kad izađete, skrenite lijevo i pogledajte natpis iznad plavih vrata.
learner.en: There's a small restaurant in the next street. When you go out, turn left and look for the sign above the blue door.

partner.en: Do we need a booking?

learner.hr: Za dvoje u ovo vrijeme obično ne, ali mogu nazvati i pitati imaju li slobodan stol.
learner.en: Usually not for two at this time, but I can call and ask whether they have a free table.

partner.hr: To bi bilo izvrsno, hvala vam.
partner.en: That would be excellent; thank you.

learner.hr: Nema na čemu. Uzmite i kartu grada, a po torbe dođite kad vam javim da je soba gotova.
learner.en: You're welcome. Take a city map too, and come back for your bags when I let you know the room is ready.

conversations.title: Guiding visitors through an old house

partner.en: Is this the start of the tour?

learner.hr: Jest. Gospodo, molim vas da prvo uđete u hodnik i ostavite dovoljno mjesta ostalim posjetiteljima.
learner.en: Yes. Gentlemen, please come into the hall first and leave enough room for the other visitors.

partner.en: Are we allowed to take photographs inside?

learner.hr: Smijete, ali bez bljeskalice. Pogledajte znak pored vrata svake prostorije jer su pravila za neke predmete drukčija.
learner.en: Yes, but without flash. Look at the sign beside each room's door, because some objects have different rules.

partner.en: How old is this house?

learner.hr: Prema našim zapisima, sagrađena je prije više od dvjesto godina. Kasnije je nekoliko puta mijenjala vlasnika.
learner.en: According to our records, it was built more than two hundred years ago. It later changed owners several times.

partner.hr: Je li namještaj iz istog razdoblja?
partner.en: Is the furniture from the same period?

learner.hr: Nije sav. Ovaj stol pripadao je prvom vlasniku, a stolice su donesene mnogo kasnije.
learner.en: Not all of it. This table belonged to the first owner, while the chairs were brought in much later.

partner.hr: Možemo li pogledati i gornji kat?
partner.en: Can we see the upper floor too?

learner.hr: Možete, samo idite polako i držite se za rukohvat. Stepenice su uske, pa ćemo se gore podijeliti u dvije grupe.
learner.en: Yes; just take your time and hold the handrail. The stairs are narrow, so we'll split into two groups upstairs.

partner.en: And where does the tour end?

learner.hr: U vrtu iza kuće. Ondje slobodno postavite dodatna pitanja ili ostanite još malo u miru.
learner.en: In the garden behind the house. Feel free to ask more questions there or stay a little longer in peace.

conversations.title: A music teacher helps a frustrated pupil

partner.hr: Zašto nikako ne mogu odsvirati ovaj dio?
partner.en: Why can't I play this part no matter what I do?

learner.hr: Zato što pokušavaš svirati prebrzo prije nego što si zapamtio pokrete. Vrati se dva reda i kreni polako.
learner.en: Because you're trying to play too fast before you've learned the movements. Go back two lines and start slowly.

partner.hr: Ali onda ne zvuči kao prava pjesma.
partner.en: But then it doesn't sound like the real song.

learner.hr: Zasad ne mora zvučati savršeno. Slušaj ritam i pusti da ti ruke nauče redoslijed tonova.
learner.en: It doesn't need to sound perfect yet. Listen to the rhythm and let your hands learn the sequence of notes.

partner.hr: Možete li mi pokazati još jednom?
partner.en: Could you show me once more?

learner.hr: Mogu. Gledaj prvo moju lijevu ruku, jer tamo preskačeš jedan ton koji je važan za cijeli dio.
learner.en: Yes. Watch my left hand first, because you're missing a note there that's important to the whole passage.

partner.en: Now I can hear the difference.

learner.hr: Dobro. Probaj ponovno, ali ne zaustavljaj se zbog svake male pogreške. Želim čuti kako povezuješ rečenicu.
learner.en: Good. Try again, but don't stop over every small mistake. I want to hear how you connect the phrase.

partner.en: Is this better?

learner.hr: Jest, puno bolje. Sačuvaj taj miran tempo i ponovi još jednom da vidiš možeš li ga zadržati.
learner.en: Yes, much better. Keep that steady tempo and repeat it once more to see whether you can maintain it.

partner.hr: Nisam mislio da ću danas uspjeti.
partner.en: I didn't think I'd manage it today.

learner.hr: Uspio si jer si promijenio način vježbanja, a ne zato što si odjednom postao netko drugi.
learner.en: You managed it because you changed how you practised, not because you suddenly became someone else.

conversations.title: Helping an older visitor find the right bus

partner.hr: Oprostite, ide li ovaj autobus prema bolnici?
partner.en: Excuse me, does this bus go towards the hospital?

learner.hr: Ne ide, gospođo. Za bolnicu trebate autobus s druge strane ceste, ali provjerimo zajedno broj na rasporedu.
learner.en: No, madam. For the hospital you need the bus across the road, but let's check the number on the timetable together.

partner.hr: Ne vidim dobro ove sitne brojeve.
partner.en: I can't see these tiny numbers very well.

learner.hr: Nema problema. Stanite ovdje u hlad, pa ću ja pročitati kada polazi sljedeći.
learner.en: No problem. Stand here in the shade, and I'll read when the next one leaves.

partner.en: Will I have a long wait?

learner.hr: Prema ovom rasporedu, deset minuta. Međutim, ne znam kasni li danas, pa pitajmo vozača kad stigne.
learner.en: According to this timetable, ten minutes. However, I don't know whether it's running late today, so let's ask the driver when it arrives.

partner.en: Do I need to buy a ticket beforehand?

learner.hr: Nisam siguran kakvo je pravilo na toj liniji. Na kiosku nam mogu dati točnu informaciju.
learner.en: I'm not sure what the rule is on that route. They can give us accurate information at the kiosk.

partner.en: I don't want to hold you up.

learner.hr: Ne zadržavate me. I moj autobus dolazi tek kasnije, pa vas mogu otpratiti do prijelaza.
learner.en: You're not holding me up. My bus isn't coming until later either, so I can walk with you to the crossing.

partner.hr: Hvala vam, baš ste mi pomogli.
partner.en: Thank you; you've really helped me.

learner.hr: Nema na čemu. Držite svoju torbu, a ja ću ponijeti ovu vrećicu dok prijeđemo cestu.
learner.en: You're welcome. Keep hold of your bag, and I'll carry this carrier bag while we cross the road.

conversations.title: Organising a noisy family dinner

partner.hr: Što trebamo napraviti prije nego što gosti dođu?
partner.en: What do we need to do before the guests arrive?

learner.hr: Dečki, prvo maknite svoje stvari sa stola. Djevojke, molim vas da donesete stolice iz druge sobe.
learner.en: Boys, first move your things off the table. Girls, please bring the chairs from the other room.

partner.en: Do we all really have to help?

learner.hr: Morate, jer večera nije samo moj posao. Svatko može učiniti nešto, čak i ako je to samo složiti salvete.
learner.en: Yes, because dinner isn't only my job. Everyone can do something, even if it's only folding napkins.

partner.en: Where do you want to put the youngest children?

learner.hr: Njih stavite bliže meni, a baki ostavite kraj stola da može lako ustati.
learner.en: Put them closer to me, and leave Grandma the end of the table so she can get up easily.

partner.en: Are these enough glasses?

learner.hr: Jest. Sad poslušajte još jednu stvar: nitko ne nosi vruće zdjele bez da prvo kaže ostalima da se maknu.
learner.en: Yes. Now listen to one more thing: nobody carries hot bowls without first telling the others to move aside.

partner.en: All right, are we finished then?

learner.hr: Skoro. Pogledajte ima li svatko pribor, pa možete izaći u dvorište dok ne pozovem na jelo.
learner.en: Nearly. Check that everyone has cutlery, then you can go into the courtyard until I call you to eat.

partner.en: Who's washing up afterwards?

learner.hr: To ćemo se dogovoriti nakon večere. Nemojte odmah nestati čim pojedete posljednji zalogaj.
learner.en: We'll agree on that after dinner. Don't all disappear the moment you eat the last mouthful.

conversations.title: Giving clear feedback on a report

partner.en: Have you looked at my report?

learner.hr: Jesam. Struktura je jasna, ali trebamo razdvojiti provjerene podatke od pretpostavki.
learner.en: Yes. The structure is clear, but we need to separate verified data from assumptions.

partner.hr: Koji dio vam je najviše zasmetao?
partner.en: Which part bothered you most?

learner.hr: Ovaj zaključak na kraju. Tvrdite da svi korisnici žele promjenu, a razgovarali smo samo s nekoliko njih.
learner.en: This conclusion at the end. You claim that all users want the change, but we've only spoken to a few of them.

partner.hr: Kako biste predložili da to napišem?
partner.en: How would you suggest I write it?

learner.hr: Napišite što su ispitanici stvarno rekli i jasno navedite koliko ih je sudjelovalo. Tako nećemo obećati više nego što znamo.
learner.en: Write what the participants actually said and clearly state how many took part. That way we won't promise more than we know.

partner.en: Should I change the tables too?

learner.hr: Da, dodajte izvor i datum uz svaku tablicu. Čitatelju treba biti jasno odakle dolaze brojevi.
learner.en: Yes; add the source and date beside each table. The reader needs to understand where the numbers come from.

partner.hr: Mogu vam poslati novu verziju sutra.
partner.en: I can send you a new version tomorrow.

learner.hr: U redu. Ako zapnete, slobodno pitajte prije nego što potrošite sate pokušavajući pogoditi što sam mislila.
learner.en: All right. If you get stuck, feel free to ask before spending hours trying to guess what I meant.

partner.hr: Hvala, sad znam što trebam popraviti.
partner.en: Thank you; now I know what I need to fix.

learner.hr: Drago mi je. Cilj je da izvještaj bude pouzdan i koristan, a ne samo da zvuči uvjerljivo.
learner.en: I'm glad. The goal is for the report to be reliable and useful, not just to sound convincing.

conversations.title: A bookseller asks what the reader enjoys

partner.hr: Tražim knjigu za prijatelja, ali ne znam koju.
partner.en: I'm looking for a book for a friend, but I don't know which one.

learner.hr: Recite mi što voli čitati. Zanima li ga više pustolovina, povijest ili neka mirnija obiteljska priča?
learner.en: Tell me what he enjoys reading. Is he more interested in adventure, history, or a quieter family story?

partner.hr: Voli priče s tajnama, ali ne voli nasilje.
partner.en: He likes stories with secrets, but he doesn't like violence.

learner.hr: Onda bih izbjegla ovu policu s mračnim trilerima. Ovdje imamo zagonetke u kojima je naglasak na likovima.
learner.en: Then I'd avoid this shelf of dark thrillers. Here we have mysteries where the focus is on the characters.

partner.hr: Kako da znam nije li knjigu već pročitao?
partner.en: How can I know whether he's already read the book?

learner.hr: Ako niste sigurni, uzmite darovni račun. Tako je može zamijeniti, a ne mora vam reći da ima isti primjerak.
learner.en: If you're unsure, take a gift receipt. That way he can exchange it without having to tell you he has the same copy.

partner.en: May I read a few pages?

learner.hr: Naravno. Sjednite ovdje i pogledajte odgovara li vam stil. Opis na koricama ne govori sve o načinu pisanja.
learner.en: Of course. Sit here and see whether you like the style. The blurb on the cover doesn't tell you everything about the writing.

partner.hr: Ova mi se čini kao dobar izbor.
partner.en: This one seems like a good choice.

learner.hr: Dobro. Želite li da je zamotamo ili biste radije sami dodali posvetu prije toga?
learner.en: Good. Would you like us to wrap it, or would you rather add a personal message yourself first?

partner.en: I'll write a message first.

learner.hr: Izvolite olovku. Ne morate napisati mnogo; nekoliko iskrenih riječi često znači više od dugog govora.
learner.en: Here's a pen. You don't need to write much; a few sincere words often mean more than a long speech.

conversations.title: A café is about to close

partner.en: Can we still get coffee?

learner.hr: Možete, ali zatvaramo za deset minuta. Ako vam odgovara, mogu je pripremiti za van.
learner.en: Yes, but we're closing in ten minutes. If that suits you, I can make it to take away.

partner.hr: Htjeli smo sjesti jer smo dugo hodali.
partner.en: We wanted to sit down because we've been walking for a long time.

learner.hr: Razumijem. Možete sjesti dok pripremim piće, samo vas molim da budete spremni otići kad završimo smjenu.
learner.en: I understand. You can sit while I prepare the drinks; I just ask that you're ready to leave when we finish our shift.

partner.hr: Hoćete li nam dati i kolač?
partner.en: Could we have cake too?

learner.hr: Danas nudimo čokoladni i limunov kolač. Želite li po jedan komad ili oba ista?
learner.en: Today we have chocolate cake and lemon cake. Would you like one piece of each or two of the same?

partner.hr: Po jedan, molim. Možemo li odmah platiti?
partner.en: One of each, please. Can we pay straight away?

learner.hr: Naravno. Tako ćete poslije moći mirno krenuti, a ja ću stići pospremiti stolove.
learner.en: Of course. Then you can leave without any rush later, and I'll have time to clear the tables.

partner.hr: Oprostite, nismo vidjeli radno vrijeme na vratima.
partner.en: Sorry, we didn't see the opening hours on the door.

learner.hr: Nema problema. Samo volim reći unaprijed, da ne ispadne da vas iznenada tjeram van.
learner.en: No problem. I just like to say so beforehand, so it doesn't seem as if I'm suddenly throwing you out.

partner.en: Thank you; we won't keep you.

learner.hr: Hvala vama na razumijevanju. Ako ponovno dođete ranije, rado ću vam preporučiti i druge kolače.
learner.en: Thank you for understanding. If you come back earlier another time, I'd be happy to recommend the other cakes too.

conversations.title: Checking props for an amateur film

partner.hr: Je li sve spremno za scenu u policijskoj postaji?
partner.en: Is everything ready for the scene at the police station?

learner.hr: Još provjeravam popis rekvizita. Lažni pištolj je označen i spremljen, a na stolu su dosje i telefon.
learner.en: I'm still checking the prop list. The fake gun is labelled and put away, and the file and telephone are on the table.

partner.hr: Zašto se mora posebno provjeravati lažno oružje?
partner.en: Why does the fake weapon need a separate check?

learner.hr: Zato što ne želimo nikakvu zabunu na snimanju. Dogovorili smo da sve takve predmete drži samo zadužena osoba.
learner.en: Because we don't want any confusion during filming. We agreed that only the designated person handles objects like that.

partner.hr: Tko glumi policajca u ovoj sceni?
partner.en: Who plays the police officer in this scene?

learner.hr: Ivan. Njegova odora visi iza zastora, a značka i kapa su u kutiji s njegovim imenom.
learner.en: Ivan. His uniform is hanging behind the curtain, and his badge and cap are in the box with his name on it.

partner.en: Is anything else missing?

learner.hr: Nedostaje pismo koje detektiv treba pronaći. Ako ga nema, cijeli razgovor o dokazu neće imati smisla.
learner.en: The letter the detective needs to find is missing. Without it, the whole conversation about the evidence won't make sense.

partner.hr: Mislim da ga je glumica uzela na probu.
partner.en: I think the actress took it to rehearsal.

learner.hr: Onda je pitaj, molim te. Ne želim izraditi drugi primjerak pa kasnije u kadru imati dva različita pisma.
learner.en: Then please ask her. I don't want to make another copy and later have two different letters on camera.

partner.hr: Našao sam ga, sve je u redu.
partner.en: I've found it; everything's all right.

learner.hr: Odlično. Sad možemo pozvati ekipu i provjeriti scenu prije nego što uključimo kamere.
learner.en: Great. Now we can call the crew and check the scene before we turn on the cameras.

conversations.title: Organising a lost-phone announcement

partner.hr: Netko je ostavio telefon na klupi. Što da napravim?
partner.en: Someone's left a phone on a bench. What should I do?

learner.hr: Donesi ga do našeg stola. Objavit ćemo da je pronađen telefon, ali nećemo otkrivati sve pojedinosti.
learner.en: Bring it to our desk. We'll announce that a phone has been found, but we won't reveal all the details.

partner.hr: Zašto ne bismo rekli koje je boje?
partner.en: Why wouldn't we say what colour it is?

learner.hr: Zato da vlasnik može opisati predmet kad dođe. Ne želimo ga slučajno dati osobi kojoj ne pripada.
learner.en: So the owner can describe it when they come. We don't want to accidentally give it to someone it doesn't belong to.

partner.hr: Trebamo li pogledati poruke da nađemo ime?
partner.en: Should we look at the messages to find a name?

learner.hr: Nećemo čitati tuđe poruke. Zasad ćemo ga sigurno spremiti i pričekati da se netko javi.
learner.en: We won't read someone else's messages. For now, we'll put it somewhere safe and wait for someone to come forward.

partner.hr: Jedna žena pita je li pronađen njezin telefon.
partner.en: A woman is asking whether her phone has been found.

learner.hr: Pozovi je ovamo i zamoli da nam kaže gdje misli da ga je izgubila i kako izgleda.
learner.en: Call her over and ask her to tell us where she thinks she lost it and what it looks like.

partner.hr: Opisala je istu masku i zna sliku na zaključanom ekranu.
partner.en: She described the same case and knows the picture on the lock screen.

learner.hr: Dobro. Neka ga sama otključa, pa ćemo biti sigurniji da je njezin prije nego što ga vratimo.
learner.en: Good. Let her unlock it herself so we can be more certain it's hers before handing it back.

partner.hr: Vratili smo ga, baš je zahvalna.
partner.en: We've returned it; she's very grateful.

learner.hr: Drago mi je. Zapiši samo da je predmet vraćen, bez nepotrebnih osobnih podataka.
learner.en: I'm glad. Just record that the item was returned, without unnecessary personal details.

conversations.title: Buying fish for a family lunch

partner.en: What would you like today, madam?

learner.hr: Trebam ribu za četiri osobe, ali ne znam koju vrstu odabrati. Ne kuham je često.
learner.en: I need fish for four people, but I don't know which kind to choose. I don't cook it often.

partner.hr: Želite li cijelu ribu ili filete?
partner.en: Would you like a whole fish or fillets?

learner.hr: Radije filete. Moja djeca ne vole tražiti sitne kosti tijekom jela.
learner.en: Fillets, preferably. My children don't like looking for tiny bones while eating.

partner.hr: Ovi su stigli jutros. Koliko želite?
partner.en: These arrived this morning. How much would you like?

learner.hr: Pokažite mi prvo otprilike koliko bi nam trebalo. Radije bih uzela malo manje i pripremila više povrća.
learner.en: Show me roughly how much we'd need first. I'd rather take a little less and prepare more vegetables.

partner.en: This much might suit you.

learner.hr: Dobro. Kolika je ukupna cijena? Nisam sigurna jesam li dobro pročitala cijenu po kilogramu.
learner.en: All right. What's the total price? I'm not sure I've read the price per kilogram correctly.

partner.en: The scale shows eight euros altogether.

learner.hr: U redu, uzet ću to. Molim vas da dobro zamotate, jer još moram kratko stati kod pekarnice.
learner.en: All right, I'll take it. Please wrap it well because I still need to stop briefly at the bakery.

partner.en: Here you are; thank you.

learner.hr: Hvala i vama. Ako ručak uspije, možda napokon prestanem zaobilaziti ovaj dio tržnice.
learner.en: Thank you too. If lunch turns out well, maybe I'll finally stop avoiding this part of the market.

conversations.title: An unexpected find during a beach clean-up

partner.en: What have you found among the stones?

learner.hr: Staru plastičnu igračku i komadiće mreže. Sve je zapelo između stijena, pa se jedva vidjelo.
learner.en: An old plastic toy and pieces of net. Everything was caught between the rocks, so it was barely visible.

partner.hr: Imaš li dovoljno mjesta u vreći?
partner.en: Have you got enough room in your bag?

learner.hr: Još malo. Kad je napunim, odnijet ću je do kombija i uzeti novu.
learner.en: A little more. When I fill it, I'll take it to the van and get another one.

partner.hr: Znaš li tko dolazi po skupljeni otpad?
partner.en: Do you know who's collecting the rubbish we've gathered?

learner.hr: Organizator je dogovorio prijevoz. Mi trebamo odvojiti ono što možemo prepoznati i ostalo prepustiti zaduženoj ekipi.
learner.en: The organiser has arranged transport. We need to separate what we can identify and leave the rest to the team in charge.

partner.hr: Nevjerojatno je koliko se toga nakupilo.
partner.en: It's incredible how much has built up.

learner.hr: Jest. Kad gledaš plažu izdaleka, izgleda čisto, a izbliza vidiš plastiku gotovo posvuda.
learner.en: Yes. From a distance the beach looks clean, but close up you see plastic almost everywhere.

partner.en: Will you stay until the end?

learner.hr: Hoću. Poslije planiram plivati, ali prvo želim završiti dio obale koji smo preuzeli.
learner.en: Yes. I'm planning to swim afterwards, but first I want to finish the stretch of coast we've taken on.

partner.en: Then I'll bring more gloves.

learner.hr: Donesi i vodu, molim te. Na ovoj vrućini više pijem nego što pričam, što je za mene prilično neobično.
learner.en: Bring water too, please. In this heat I'm drinking more than I'm talking, which is fairly unusual for me.

conversations.title: A proposal to save an old cinema

partner.en: Why are you collecting signatures outside the cinema?

learner.hr: Želimo sačuvati zgradu. Vlasnik je planira prodati, a mi bismo voljeli da prostor ostane dostupan zajednici.
learner.en: We want to preserve the building. The owner plans to sell it, and we'd like the space to stay available to the community.

partner.hr: Ali ovdje već dugo nema projekcija.
partner.en: But there haven't been screenings here for a long time.

learner.hr: Točno. Predlažemo da se dvorana koristi i za predstave, predavanja i školske nastupe, a ne samo za filmove.
learner.en: That's right. We suggest using the hall for plays, talks and school performances too, not just films.

partner.en: Who would pay for the renovation?

learner.hr: To još istražujemo. Zasad imamo prijedlog i zainteresirane susjede, a ne gotov plan s izračunatim troškovima.
learner.en: We're still looking into that. So far we have a proposal and interested neighbours, rather than a finished plan with calculated costs.

partner.hr: Hoćete li razgovarati s gradskim vijećem?
partner.en: Will you speak to the city council?

learner.hr: Hoćemo. Pripremamo podatke o stanju zgrade i o tome koliko bi se ljudi uključilo u program.
learner.en: Yes. We're preparing information about the building's condition and how many people would take part in the programme.

partner.hr: Mogu li se i ja uključiti?
partner.en: Can I get involved too?

learner.hr: Naravno. Ostavite kontakt ako želite primati obavijesti, ili dođite na otvoreni sastanak u petak.
learner.en: Of course. Leave a contact if you'd like updates, or come to the open meeting on Friday.

partner.hr: Doći ću. Ovdje sam gledao svoj prvi film.
partner.en: I'll come. I saw my first film here.

learner.hr: Onda imate i priču koju vrijedi čuti. Želimo sačuvati uspomene, ali i pronaći smisao za budućnost zgrade.
learner.en: Then you have a story worth hearing too. We want to preserve the memories, but also find a purpose for the building's future.

conversations.title: Visiting a church that matters to a grandmother

partner.hr: Hoćeš li ući sa mnom u crkvu?
partner.en: Will you come into the church with me?

learner.hr: Hoću, bako. Nisam dugo bio unutra, ali znam da ti ovo mjesto puno znači.
learner.en: Yes, Grandma. I haven't been inside for a long time, but I know this place means a lot to you.

partner.hr: Tu sam se udala za tvog djeda.
partner.en: This is where I married your grandfather.

learner.hr: Stvarno? Mislio sam da je vjenčanje bilo u selu u kojem si odrasla.
learner.en: Really? I thought the wedding was in the village where you grew up.

partner.hr: Ne, tada smo već oboje radili ovdje.
partner.en: No, by then we were both working here.

learner.hr: Sad razumijem. Sjećaš li se tko vas je fotografirao pred ulazom? Ta slika još visi u hodniku.
learner.en: Now I understand. Do you remember who photographed you outside the entrance? That picture still hangs in the hall.

partner.en: Your grandfather's brother took it.

learner.hr: Nisam znao da je i on bio tamo. Volio bih da mi jednom pokažeš sve ljude na toj slici.
learner.en: I didn't know he was there too. I'd like you to show me who everyone in that picture is sometime.

partner.hr: Možemo poslije, sad ću kratko sjesti.
partner.en: We can afterwards; I'll sit for a little while now.

learner.hr: U redu. Ja ću biti pored tebe, a poslije možemo zapaliti svijeću ako to želiš.
learner.en: All right. I'll be beside you, and afterwards we can light a candle if you'd like.

partner.hr: Drago mi je što si došao, iako ne vjeruješ isto što i ja.
partner.en: I'm glad you came even though you don't share my beliefs.

learner.hr: I meni je drago. Ne moramo imati istu vjeru da bismo poštovali ono što je drugome važno.
learner.en: I'm glad too. We don't have to share the same faith to respect what matters to each other.

conversations.title: Laundry is stuck in a broken machine

partner.hr: Zašto je rublje još u perilici?
partner.en: Why is the laundry still in the washing machine?

learner.hr: Stroj je stao usred programa i vrata se ne otvaraju. Već sam nazvala servis.
learner.en: The machine stopped halfway through the programme, and the door won't open. I've already called the repair service.

partner.en: When can they come?

learner.hr: Sutra ujutro. Rekli su da ništa ne pokušavam silom, pa sam ostavila sve kako jest.
learner.en: Tomorrow morning. They said not to force anything, so I've left everything as it is.

partner.hr: A što ćeš obući na posao?
partner.en: What will you wear to work?

learner.hr: Imam drugu košulju, ali hlače koje sam planirala nositi zarobljene su unutra.
learner.en: I've got another shirt, but the trousers I planned to wear are trapped inside.

partner.hr: Možeš uzeti moje ako ti odgovaraju.
partner.en: You can borrow mine if they fit.

learner.hr: Hvala, ali preduge su mi. Izgledala bih kao dijete koje se presvuklo u tuđu odjeću.
learner.en: Thanks, but they're too long. I'd look like a child dressed in someone else's clothes.

partner.en: Shall I take you shopping, then?

learner.hr: Ne treba. Pronaći ću nešto u ormaru, samo moram prestati gledati u perilicu kao da će me poslušati.
learner.en: No need. I'll find something in the wardrobe; I just need to stop staring at the washing machine as if it'll listen to me.

partner.en: Maybe it needs a kind word.

learner.hr: Vjeruj mi, nakon svih ružnih riječi koje je danas čula, jedna lijepa ne bi puno promijenila.
learner.en: Believe me, after all the unkind words it's heard today, one kind word wouldn't change much.

conversations.title: Sharing a basketball court with younger children

partner.en: Will you be playing much longer?

learner.hr: Planirali smo još pola sata. Želite li poslije koristiti cijeli teren ili vam je dovoljan jedan koš?
learner.en: We'd planned another half an hour. Would you like to use the whole court afterwards, or is one hoop enough?

partner.hr: Nama je jedan dovoljan, djeca tek uče.
partner.en: One is enough for us; the children are just learning.

learner.hr: Onda se možemo podijeliti odmah. Naša ekipa prijeći će na drugu stranu i igrati na jedan koš.
learner.en: Then we can split it now. Our team can move to the other side and play with one hoop.

partner.en: We don't want to spoil your game.

learner.hr: Nećete. I mi smo nekad bili klinci koji nisu mogli dobaciti loptu dovoljno visoko.
learner.en: You won't. We were kids who couldn't throw the ball high enough once too.

partner.hr: Moj sin misli da će odmah postati najbolji.
partner.en: My son thinks he'll be the best straight away.

learner.hr: Recite mu da je i meni trebalo mnogo pokušaja za prvi pogodak. Nije sramota promašiti dok učiš.
learner.en: Tell him it took me lots of attempts to score my first basket too. There's no shame in missing while you're learning.

partner.hr: Smiju li vas malo gledati kad završimo?
partner.en: Can they watch you for a while when we finish?

learner.hr: Smiju, samo neka ostanu izvan crte da se ne sudarimo dok trčimo. Poslije im možemo pokazati jednostavnu vježbu.
learner.en: Yes; just have them stay outside the line so we don't bump into them while running. Afterwards we can show them a simple drill.

partner.en: That's very kind of you; thank you.

learner.hr: Nema na čemu. Draže mi je vidjeti teren pun ljudi nego ga čuvati praznog samo za sebe.
learner.en: You're welcome. I'd rather see a court full of people than keep it empty just for myself.

conversations.title: A city child visits a family farm

partner.hr: Smijem li prići onom velikom konju?
partner.en: May I go up to that big horse?

learner.hr: Pitaj prvo ujaka, on poznaje životinje. Ja ne znam želi li konj trenutno društvo.
learner.en: Ask our uncle first; he knows the animals. I don't know whether the horse wants company right now.

partner.hr: Mislio sam da ti znaš sve o farmi.
partner.en: I thought you knew everything about the farm.

learner.hr: Ne znam, samo sam ovdje provodio ljeta kao dijete. Tada sam više gledao nego pomagao.
learner.en: I don't; I just spent summers here as a child. Back then I watched more than I helped.

partner.hr: A čime si se najviše volio baviti?
partner.en: What did you enjoy doing most?

learner.hr: Volio sam skupljati jaja i tražiti mačke po dvorištu. Krave su mi izgledale ogromno pa sam ih radije promatrao izdaleka.
learner.en: I liked collecting eggs and looking for cats around the yard. The cows looked enormous to me, so I preferred watching them from a distance.

partner.en: Did you ever drive the tractor?

learner.hr: Nisam sam. Sjedio sam pored djeda i pravio se da sam važan vozač, dok je on radio sav posao.
learner.en: Not by myself. I sat beside Grandad and pretended to be an important driver while he did all the work.

partner.hr: Misliš li da će mi ujak pokazati staju?
partner.en: Do you think our uncle will show me the stable?

learner.hr: Mislim da hoće, kad završi hranjenje. Nemoj ga požurivati, jer njemu ovo nije samo izlet nego svakodnevni posao.
learner.en: I think so, once he's finished feeding the animals. Don't rush him, because for him this isn't just an outing but everyday work.

partner.en: All right, I'll wait here.

learner.hr: Dođi pod drvo da sjednemo. Možda do tada neka mačka sama odluči da smo dovoljno zanimljivi.
learner.en: Come and sit under the tree. Maybe by then a cat will decide for itself that we're interesting enough.

conversations.title: A room looks different from its photographs

partner.hr: Kako ti se čini soba koju smo došli pogledati?
partner.en: What do you think of the room we've come to see?

learner.hr: Iskreno, mnogo je manja nego na fotografijama. Nisam očekivala da će krevet zauzimati gotovo cijeli prostor.
learner.en: Honestly, it's much smaller than in the photographs. I didn't expect the bed to take up almost all the space.

partner.en: Maybe you could move the desk.

learner.hr: Mogla bih, ali tada ne bih mogla potpuno otvoriti ormar. To nije baš praktično za svakodnevni život.
learner.en: I could, but then I wouldn't be able to open the wardrobe fully. That isn't very practical for everyday life.

partner.en: Still, the location is good.

learner.hr: Jest, blizu je fakulteta i trgovine. Ali moram uzeti u obzir i buku s ceste, ne samo udaljenost.
learner.en: Yes, it's near the university and a shop. But I have to consider the road noise too, not just the distance.

partner.hr: Hoćeš li pitati je li stanarina niža za duži najam?
partner.en: Will you ask whether the rent is lower for a longer tenancy?

learner.hr: Hoću, iako mislim da ni niža cijena ne bi riješila problem s prostorom. Ne želim pristati samo zato što smo već došli.
learner.en: Yes, although I don't think even a lower price would solve the space problem. I don't want to agree just because we've already come here.

partner.en: What will you tell the owner?

learner.hr: Zahvalit ću mu na vremenu i reći da soba ne odgovara mojim potrebama. Ne moram izmišljati izgovor.
learner.en: I'll thank him for his time and say the room doesn't meet my needs. I don't need to invent an excuse.

partner.hr: Imamo još jednu adresu za danas.
partner.en: We've got one more address to visit today.

learner.hr: Onda krenimo. Barem sad znam što mi je važnije nego što mi se činilo dok sam gledala oglase.
learner.en: Then let's go. At least now I know what matters more to me than it seemed when I was looking at adverts.

conversations.title: Choosing a subject for a short film

partner.hr: O čemu želiš snimiti svoj prvi kratki film?
partner.en: What would you like your first short film to be about?

learner.hr: O ljudima koji otvaraju grad prije nego što se ostali probude. Pekarima, čistačima i vozačima prvih autobusa.
learner.en: The people who open up the city before everyone else wakes up. Bakers, cleaners and drivers of the first buses.

partner.en: How will you get in touch with them?

learner.hr: Prvo ću pitati žele li sudjelovati. Ne želim ih samo snimati dok rade pa poslije tražiti dopuštenje.
learner.en: First I'll ask whether they'd like to take part. I don't want to just film them working and ask permission afterwards.

partner.en: Will you have a narrator?

learner.hr: Možda ne. Radije bih da sami govore o svom poslu, a ja da povežem njihove priče slikama grada.
learner.en: Maybe not. I'd rather they talked about their work themselves and I connected their stories with images of the city.

partner.hr: Što ako nitko ne želi govoriti pred kamerom?
partner.en: What if nobody wants to speak on camera?

learner.hr: Onda ću promijeniti pristup. Mogu snimiti zvukove, prazne ulice i pripreme bez prikazivanja nečijeg lica.
learner.en: Then I'll change my approach. I can record sounds, empty streets and preparations without showing anyone's face.

partner.en: When are you starting?

learner.hr: Sljedećeg tjedna. Najteži dio bit će ustati dovoljno rano, jer sam dosad grad uglavnom gledao noću.
learner.en: Next week. The hardest part will be getting up early enough, because until now I've mostly seen the city at night.

partner.en: I can help you carry the equipment.

learner.hr: Možeš, ali nemoj obećati prije nego što čuješ vrijeme polaska. Naći ćemo se u četiri ujutro.
learner.en: You can, but don't promise before you hear the departure time. We're meeting at four in the morning.

conversations.title: A band rehearsal is louder than expected

partner.hr: Čuje li se glazba jako iz našeg stana?
partner.en: Can you hear the music loudly from our flat?

learner.hr: Čuje se u cijelom hodniku. Nisam znala da kod vas večeras svira bend.
learner.en: It can be heard all along the corridor. I didn't know a band was playing at your place tonight.

partner.en: We're just practising briefly for a birthday.

learner.hr: Razumijem, ali moj sin pokušava zaspati. Možete li stišati pojačala ili završiti ranije?
learner.en: I understand, but my son is trying to sleep. Could you turn down the amplifiers or finish earlier?

partner.hr: Mislio sam da se kroz zidove ne čuje toliko.
partner.en: I thought it didn't carry through the walls so much.

learner.hr: Nažalost čuje, posebno bubnjevi. Ne tražim da nikad ne svirate, samo da se dogovorimo o vremenu.
learner.en: Unfortunately it does, especially the drums. I'm not asking you never to play, just that we agree on a time.

partner.hr: Oprosti, odmah ćemo prestati s bubnjevima.
partner.en: Sorry; we'll stop the drums right away.

learner.hr: Hvala ti. Ako planirate još koju probu, javi dan ranije pa možemo pronaći termin koji svima odgovara.
learner.en: Thank you. If you're planning another rehearsal, let me know a day beforehand so we can find a time that works for everyone.

partner.hr: Hoće li subota popodne biti bolja?
partner.en: Would Saturday afternoon be better?

learner.hr: Hoće, tada smo obično vani. Ali za cijeli bend možda je ipak bolja prostorija koja je namijenjena probama.
learner.en: Yes; we're usually out then. But a room intended for rehearsals may still be better for a whole band.

partner.hr: Pitat ću ostale možemo li je unajmiti.
partner.en: I'll ask the others whether we can hire one.

learner.hr: Odlično. Rado ću vas doći slušati na rođendan, samo bih večeras radije čula tišinu.
learner.en: Great. I'd be happy to come and listen at the birthday; I'd just rather hear silence tonight.

conversations.title: A piano will not fit through the doorway

partner.hr: Može li klavir proći kroz ova vrata?
partner.en: Can the piano fit through this doorway?

learner.hr: Ovako ne može. Izmjerio sam otvor, ali sam zaboravio da se vrata ne otvaraju do kraja.
learner.en: Not like this. I measured the opening, but I forgot the door doesn't open all the way.

partner.en: Shall we try turning it?

learner.hr: Pričekajmo ljude iz selidbene službe. Oni su preuzeli posao i znaju kako sigurno premjestiti tako težak predmet.
learner.en: Let's wait for the movers. They've taken on the job and know how to move something so heavy safely.

partner.hr: Gdje da ostavim ove kutije dok čekamo?
partner.en: Where should I leave these boxes while we wait?

learner.hr: Odnesi ih u drugu sobu i ostavi hodnik prazan. Trebat će im dovoljno prostora s obje strane.
learner.en: Take them into the other room and leave the hallway empty. They'll need enough room on both sides.

partner.en: Did you at least measure the stairs?

learner.hr: Jesam, i poslao sam fotografije. Jedino ova vrata nisam pokazao jer mi se činilo da tu nema problema.
learner.en: Yes, and I sent photographs. This door was the only thing I didn't show because I thought it wouldn't be a problem.

partner.hr: Možda će trebati doći drugi put.
partner.en: They might need to come back another time.

learner.hr: Možda, ali radije bih čekao nego oštetio klavir koji je pripadao mojoj majci.
learner.en: Maybe, but I'd rather wait than damage the piano that belonged to my mother.

partner.en: Here they are at the entrance.

learner.hr: Dobro. Idem im odmah reći što sam pogriješio, prije nego što krenu nositi išta iz kamiona.
learner.en: Good. I'll tell them what I got wrong straight away, before they start carrying anything out of the truck.

conversations.title: Choosing an older cat at a shelter

partner.hr: Većina posjetitelja prvo pita za mačiće.
partner.en: Most visitors ask about kittens first.

learner.hr: Znam, ali mene zanima ova starija mačka. Čini se mirna, a ja živim u malom stanu.
learner.en: I know, but I'm interested in this older cat. She seems calm, and I live in a small flat.

partner.hr: Ona se sporije navikava na nove ljude.
partner.en: She takes longer to get used to new people.

learner.hr: To mi ne smeta. I ja trebam vremena kad dođem u nepoznato okruženje.
learner.en: I don't mind that. I need time too when I arrive somewhere unfamiliar.

partner.hr: Jeste li prije imali kućnog ljubimca?
partner.en: Have you had a pet before?

learner.hr: Jesam, ali davno. Voljela bih čuti kakve navike ima i što joj je važno za svakodnevni život.
learner.en: Yes, but a long time ago. I'd like to hear about her habits and what matters to her in everyday life.

partner.hr: Voli mir i svoje mjesto pored prozora.
partner.en: She likes peace and having her own place by a window.

learner.hr: Takvo mjesto imam. Samo ne bih htjela pretpostaviti da će odmah biti sretna kod mene.
learner.en: I've got a spot like that. I just wouldn't want to assume she'll immediately be happy with me.

partner.hr: Možete je posjetiti još nekoliko puta prije odluke.
partner.en: You can visit her a few more times before deciding.

learner.hr: To bih rado. Važnije mi je da joj odgovaram nego da danas odem kući s bilo kojom mačkom.
learner.en: I'd like that. It's more important to me that I'm a good match for her than that I go home with just any cat today.

partner.en: Then let's arrange your next visit.

learner.hr: Može. U međuvremenu ću pripremiti stan i zapisati pitanja koja mi sada nisu pala na pamet.
learner.en: Yes. Meanwhile I'll prepare the flat and write down any questions I haven't thought of now.

conversations.title: Deciding whether to run for class representative

partner.hr: Zašto nisi prijavio kandidaturu za predstavnika razreda?
partner.en: Why haven't you put yourself forward as class representative?

learner.hr: Nisam siguran da sam pravi kandidat. Nisam najglasniji i ne volim obećavati stvari koje ne mogu ispuniti.
learner.en: I'm not sure I'm the right candidate. I'm not the loudest, and I don't like promising things I can't deliver.

partner.hr: Ne moraš biti najglasniji da bi dobro slušao.
partner.en: You don't have to be the loudest to listen well.

learner.hr: To je istina. Volio bih da se u vijeću čuje i mišljenje učenika koji se rijetko javljaju.
learner.en: That's true. I'd like the council to hear the opinions of pupils who rarely speak up too.

partner.hr: Što bi predložio kao prvi cilj?
partner.en: What would you suggest as the first goal?

learner.hr: Da unaprijed skupljamo pitanja prije svakog sastanka. Tako se ne bi sve svelo na ono što se meni taj dan sjetilo.
learner.en: That we collect questions before every meeting. That way it wouldn't all come down to whatever I happen to think of that day.

partner.hr: Kako bi objasnio to u svom govoru?
partner.en: How would you explain that in your speech?

learner.hr: Jednostavno. Rekao bih da ne mogu odlučivati umjesto svih, nego prenositi ono o čemu se zajedno dogovorimo.
learner.en: Simply. I'd say I can't make decisions for everyone, but can pass on what we've agreed together.

partner.hr: Onda mislim da već imaš dobar početak.
partner.en: Then I think you've already got a good start.

learner.hr: Možda. Izbori su tek sljedeći tjedan, pa imam vremena pitati ostale što očekuju od predstavnika.
learner.en: Maybe. The election isn't until next week, so I've got time to ask the others what they expect from a representative.

partner.en: Will you put yourself forward after all?

learner.hr: Hoću. A ako ne pobijedim, svejedno mogu pomoći osobi koju razred odabere.
learner.en: Yes. And if I don't win, I can still help whoever the class chooses.

conversations.title: Two sources give different dates

partner.hr: Zašto u svom radu navodiš dvije godine za isti događaj?
partner.en: Why do you list two years for the same event in your paper?

learner.hr: Zato što se izvori ne slažu. U novinama piše jedna godina, a u općinskom zapisu druga.
learner.en: Because the sources disagree. The newspaper gives one year, and the municipal record gives another.

partner.hr: Možda je u jednome samo pogreška.
partner.en: Maybe one of them just has a mistake.

learner.hr: Moguće, ali ne mogu odabrati datum samo zato što mi se jedan izvor više sviđa.
learner.en: Possibly, but I can't choose a date just because I like one source more.

partner.en: Is there another document?

learner.hr: U arhivu imaju pismo iz tog razdoblja. Zamolila sam da mi dopuste pogledati izvornik, jer je kopija slabo čitljiva.
learner.en: The archive has a letter from that period. I've asked for permission to see the original because the copy is hard to read.

partner.hr: Što ako ni nakon toga ne bude jasno?
partner.en: What if it still isn't clear after that?

learner.hr: Onda ću napisati da datum nije pouzdano utvrđen i objasniti na čemu temeljim takav zaključak.
learner.en: Then I'll write that the date hasn't been established reliably and explain the basis for that conclusion.

partner.hr: Neće li rad tako zvučati nedovršeno?
partner.en: Won't that make the paper sound unfinished?

learner.hr: Možda će zvučati manje sigurno, ali bit će točniji. Nije isto ne znati i pretvarati se da znaš.
learner.en: It might sound less certain, but it'll be more accurate. Not knowing isn't the same as pretending you know.

partner.en: When are you going back to the archive?

learner.hr: U srijedu. Ako nađem nešto novo, prvo ću usporediti cijeli sadržaj, a ne samo broj koji tražim.
learner.en: On Wednesday. If I find something new, I'll compare the whole contents first, not just the number I'm looking for.

conversations.title: A tie refuses to cooperate

partner.hr: Zašto još nisi spreman za večeru?
partner.en: Why aren't you ready for dinner yet?

learner.hr: Zato što pokušavam zavezati kravatu koju nisam nosio godinama. Čvor izgleda kao malo gnijezdo.
learner.en: Because I'm trying to tie a tie I haven't worn for years. The knot looks like a little nest.

partner.en: Would you like me to help?

learner.hr: Molim te. Samo me nemoj pitati kako sam to prije znao, jer se ni sam ne sjećam.
learner.en: Please. Just don't ask how I used to know how to do this, because I don't remember either.

partner.hr: Stani ravno i okreni se prema ogledalu.
partner.en: Stand straight and turn towards the mirror.

learner.hr: Evo. Sad barem vidim koliko mi je košulja zgužvana. Očito kravata nije jedini problem.
learner.en: There. Now I can at least see how creased my shirt is. Clearly the tie isn't the only problem.

partner.hr: Imamo još vremena da je promijeniš.
partner.en: We've still got time for you to change it.

learner.hr: Imam jednu bijelu u ormaru. Možeš li pogledati visi li na vješalici iza mog odijela?
learner.en: I've got a white one in the wardrobe. Can you check whether it's hanging behind my suit?

partner.hr: Tu je, i već je izglačana.
partner.en: Here it is, and it's already ironed.

learner.hr: Odlično. Ako uspijemo izaći na vrijeme, zasluga je potpuno tvoja, a ne moj smisao za pripremu.
learner.en: Great. If we manage to leave on time, the credit is entirely yours rather than my talent for preparation.

partner.en: Get ready earlier next time.

learner.hr: Hoću. Ili ću birati događaje na kojima se od mene očekuje samo čista majica, a ne diplomatski izgled.
learner.en: I will. Or I'll choose events where all that's expected of me is a clean T-shirt rather than a diplomatic appearance.

conversations.title: An inherited clock at a repair shop

partner.hr: Što nije u redu sa satom?
partner.en: What's wrong with the clock?

learner.hr: Prestao je raditi prošli mjesec. Prije toga je kasnio, ali nisam odmah shvatio da postoji ozbiljniji kvar.
learner.en: It stopped working last month. Before that it was running slow, but I didn't immediately realise there was a more serious fault.

partner.en: Do you know how old it is?

learner.hr: Ne znam točno. Pripadao je mom djedu, a prije njega njegovu ocu. U obitelji je već dugo.
learner.en: I don't know exactly. It belonged to my grandfather, and to his father before him. It's been in the family a long time.

partner.hr: Želite li i obnoviti vanjski izgled?
partner.en: Would you like the exterior restored too?

learner.hr: Samo koliko je potrebno da ostane čitav. Ne bih htio ukloniti svaku ogrebotinu i izgubiti tragove njegove prošlosti.
learner.en: Only as much as necessary to keep it intact. I wouldn't want to remove every scratch and lose the traces of its past.

partner.hr: Moram ga otvoriti prije procjene troška.
partner.en: I need to open it before estimating the cost.

learner.hr: Razumijem. Javite mi iznos prije popravka, pa ću odlučiti mogu li ga sada priuštiti.
learner.en: I understand. Let me know the amount before repairing it, and I'll decide whether I can afford it now.

partner.hr: Važnija vam je uspomena nego vrijednost sata?
partner.en: Does the memory matter more to you than the clock's value?

learner.hr: Jest. Novi sat mogu kupiti bilo gdje, ali ovaj me podsjeća na sobu u kojoj sam slušao djedove priče.
learner.en: Yes. I can buy a new clock anywhere, but this one reminds me of the room where I listened to my grandfather's stories.

partner.hr: Nazvat ću vas kad ga pregledam.
partner.en: I'll call you once I've examined it.

learner.hr: Hvala vam. Ako ga uspijete popraviti, bit će mi drago opet čuti isti zvuk u svojoj kući.
learner.en: Thank you. If you can repair it, I'll be glad to hear that same sound in my own house again.

conversations.title: Writing clues for a birthday treasure hunt

partner.hr: Koliko tragova trebamo sakriti za djecu?
partner.en: How many clues should we hide for the children?

learner.hr: Šest bi trebalo biti dovoljno. Prvi ćemo staviti ispod stola, a posljednji vodi do kutije s blagom.
learner.en: Six should be enough. We'll put the first under the table, and the last leads to the treasure box.

partner.en: Are the riddles too difficult?

learner.hr: Ova o sjeni možda jest. Najmlađi još ne čitaju dobro, pa trebamo i slike, ne samo tekst.
learner.en: The one about the shadow might be. The youngest children aren't confident readers yet, so we need pictures as well as text.

partner.en: What shall we put in the box?

learner.hr: Male naljepnice i po jednu čokoladicu za svakoga. Ne želim da najbrži uzmu sve prije ostalih.
learner.en: Little stickers and one small chocolate each. I don't want the fastest children to take everything before the others.

partner.hr: Hoćemo li ih podijeliti u dvije ekipe?
partner.en: Shall we split them into two teams?

learner.hr: Radije neka svi traže zajedno. Stariji mogu čitati, a mlađi pronalaziti predmete na slikama.
learner.en: I'd rather they all looked together. The older ones can read, and the younger ones can find the objects in the pictures.

partner.hr: A ako odmah pronađu kutiju slučajno?
partner.en: What if they find the box straight away by accident?

learner.hr: Onda ćemo se praviti da je to prazan kovčeg i zamoliti ih da prvo riješe ostale tragove.
learner.en: Then we'll pretend it's an empty chest and ask them to solve the other clues first.

partner.hr: Nadam se da nam plan neće propasti.
partner.en: I hope our plan doesn't fall apart.

learner.hr: Čak i ako propadne, djeca će se vjerojatno zabaviti. Samo mi nemoj zaboraviti gdje smo stvarno sakrili blago.
learner.en: Even if it does, the children will probably have fun. Just don't let me forget where we've actually hidden the treasure.

conversations.title: Was that invitation meant as a date?

partner.hr: Zašto izgledaš tako zbunjeno nakon kave?
partner.en: Why do you look so confused after coffee?

learner.hr: Nisam sigurna je li to bio spoj ili samo druženje. Razgovarali smo dva sata, ali nitko nije ništa jasno rekao.
learner.en: I'm not sure whether it was a date or just hanging out. We talked for two hours, but nobody said anything clearly.

partner.hr: Jesi li ti htjela da bude spoj?
partner.en: Did you want it to be a date?

learner.hr: Jesam. Sviđa mi se, ali ne želim iz svakog osmijeha zaključivati da osjeća isto.
learner.en: Yes. I like him, but I don't want to read every smile as proof that he feels the same.

partner.en: Can you simply ask him?

learner.hr: Mogu, samo mi je neugodno. Lakše mi je smišljati deset tumačenja nego izgovoriti jedno pitanje.
learner.en: I can; I just feel awkward. It's easier for me to invent ten interpretations than ask one question aloud.

partner.hr: Što bi ga zapravo htjela pitati?
partner.en: What would you actually like to ask him?

learner.hr: Bi li htio izaći sa mnom opet, ovaj put na pravi spoj. Tako barem neće morati pogoditi što mislim.
learner.en: Whether he'd like to go out with me again, this time on a proper date. At least then he won't have to guess what I mean.

partner.hr: A ako kaže da želi samo prijateljstvo?
partner.en: And if he says he only wants friendship?

learner.hr: Bit će mi žao, ali barem ću znati. Ne želim ga uvjeravati da mora osjećati nešto drukčije.
learner.en: I'll be disappointed, but at least I'll know. I don't want to persuade him that he has to feel differently.

partner.en: Will you send a message tonight?

learner.hr: Hoću. Samo ću je prvo skratiti, jer sam umjesto pitanja već napisala pola ljubavnog romana.
learner.en: Yes. I'll just shorten it first, because I've already written half a romance novel instead of a question.

conversations.title: Wedding photographs in unexpected rain

partner.hr: Što ćemo ako i dalje bude padala kiša?
partner.en: What will we do if it keeps raining?

learner.hr: Fotografije možemo snimiti u velikom hodniku. Ima dovoljno svjetla, a gosti neće morati stajati mokri u vrtu.
learner.en: We can take the photographs in the large hallway. There's enough light, and the guests won't have to stand getting wet in the garden.

partner.hr: Ali mladenka je željela slike ispred ruža.
partner.en: But the bride wanted pictures in front of the roses.

learner.hr: Znam. Reći ću joj koje su mogućnosti i pustiti da sama odluči želi li pričekati kratku stanku u kiši.
learner.en: I know. I'll explain the options and let her decide whether she wants to wait for a brief break in the rain.

partner.hr: Možeš li kasnije snimiti samo njih dvoje vani?
partner.en: Can you photograph just the two of them outside later?

learner.hr: Mogu. Ostale ćemo fotografirati prvo, posebno starije goste i djecu koja su već umorna.
learner.en: Yes. We'll photograph the others first, especially the older guests and the children who are already tired.

partner.hr: Trebaš li nekoga da ti pomogne s rasporedom?
partner.en: Do you need someone to help organise everyone?

learner.hr: Trebam. Molim te, pozovi obitelji redom, ali nemoj vikati preko cijele dvorane.
learner.en: Yes. Please call the families in order, but don't shout across the whole hall.

partner.hr: Hoće li kiša pokvariti konačne fotografije?
partner.en: Will the rain spoil the final photographs?

learner.hr: Ne mora. Fotografije trebaju pokazati njihov dan, a taj dan jednostavno ima i kišu.
learner.en: Not necessarily. The photographs should show their day, and that day simply includes rain.

partner.en: All right; I'll fetch the first group.

learner.hr: Hvala. Reci im da ne trebaju svi izgledati ozbiljno, ovo je vjenčanje, a ne slikanje za dokumente.
learner.en: Thank you. Tell them they don't all need to look solemn; this is a wedding, not an identity photograph.

conversations.title: A model bridge bends under its first test

partner.hr: Zašto se naš most savio već pod prvom knjigom?
partner.en: Why did our bridge bend under the very first book?

learner.hr: Mislim da smo previše pažnje posvetili izgledu, a premalo načinu na koji nosi težinu.
learner.en: I think we paid too much attention to its appearance and too little to how it carries weight.

partner.en: Can we add more glue?

learner.hr: Možemo, ali prvo trebamo shvatiti koji dio popušta. Inače ćemo samo zalijepiti istu pogrešku čvršće.
learner.en: We can, but first we need to understand which part is giving way. Otherwise we'll just glue the same mistake more firmly.

partner.hr: Ovdje na sredini sve se pomaknulo.
partner.en: Everything moved here in the middle.

learner.hr: Vidim. Oslonci s obje strane ostali su na mjestu, pa možda trebamo drukčije povezati srednje dijelove.
learner.en: I see. The supports on both sides stayed in place, so perhaps we need to connect the middle sections differently.

partner.hr: Hoćemo li pitati učitelja za pomoć?
partner.en: Shall we ask the teacher for help?

learner.hr: Hoćemo. Ne mora nam dati rješenje, može nam pokazati što trebamo promatrati tijekom sljedećeg testa.
learner.en: Yes. He doesn't have to give us the solution; he can show us what to watch during the next test.

partner.hr: Moramo li priznati da je prvi pokušaj propao?
partner.en: Do we have to admit the first attempt failed?

learner.hr: Moramo. Fotografirat ćemo ga i zapisati što se dogodilo. I to je dio našeg projekta.
learner.en: Yes. We'll photograph it and record what happened. That's part of our project too.

partner.hr: A ako drugi put opet padne?
partner.en: What if it collapses again the second time?

learner.hr: Onda ćemo barem znati je li pao na isti način. Za sada smo izgradili vrlo lijep stalak za jednu laganu olovku.
learner.en: Then at least we'll know whether it collapsed the same way. For now we've built a very pretty stand for one light pencil.

conversations.title: A meeting on the wrong floor

partner.en: Where are you? Everyone's waiting.

learner.hr: Ispred ureda, ali vrata su zaključana.
learner.en: Outside the office, but the door's locked.

partner.en: Which floor are you on?

learner.hr: Na trećem. Zar sastanak nije ovdje?
learner.en: The third. Isn't the meeting here?

partner.en: We've moved to the fourth.

learner.hr: Nitko mi nije javio. Odmah dolazim gore.
learner.en: Nobody told me. I'm coming up now.

partner.en: The message is in the group.

learner.hr: Sad je vidim. Utišao sam obavijesti.
learner.en: I see it now. I muted the notifications.

partner.en: We haven't started yet.

learner.hr: Dobro. Onda nisam zakasnio, samo sam zalutao.
learner.en: Good. Then I'm not late, just lost.

conversations.title: Something left in a borrowed jacket

partner.en: Have you returned my jacket?

learner.hr: Jesam, ali tvoju narukvicu još imam.
learner.en: Yes, but I still have your bracelet.

partner.en: What bracelet?

learner.hr: Srebrnu. Bila je u unutarnjem džepu.
learner.en: A silver one. It was in the inside pocket.

partner.en: I thought it was lost!

learner.hr: Onda sam dobro učinila što sam provjerila džepove.
learner.en: Then it's a good thing I checked the pockets.

partner.en: Can you bring it tonight?

learner.hr: Mogu. Stavila sam je u malu kutiju.
learner.en: Yes. I've put it in a little box.

partner.en: Thank you, dear.

learner.hr: Nema na čemu. Jakna je očito čuvala tajnu.
learner.en: You're welcome. The jacket was clearly keeping a secret.

conversations.title: Meeting a dog in the lift

partner.hr: Smeta li vam pas u dizalu?
partner.en: Do you mind the dog in the lift?

learner.hr: Ne smeta, samo mi je malo neobično koliko je velik.
learner.en: No; I'm just surprised by how big he is.

partner.en: He's very calm.

learner.hr: Vidim. Gleda me kao da me već poznaje.
learner.en: I see. He's looking at me as if he already knows me.

partner.en: He's noticed your bag.

learner.hr: Aha, u njoj nosim meso za ručak.
learner.en: Ah, I'm carrying meat for lunch in it.

partner.en: That's why he's watching you so closely.

learner.hr: Znači, nije ljubav nego zanimanje za hranu.
learner.en: So it isn't love, just an interest in food.

partner.hr: Često je to kod njega isto.
partner.en: For him those are often the same thing.

learner.hr: Onda ćemo se slagati. I meni ručak puno znači.
learner.en: Then we'll get along. Lunch matters a lot to me too.

conversations.title: A concert ticket for the wrong evening

partner.en: Shall we leave for the concert?

learner.hr: Čekaj, na mojoj karti piše subota.
learner.en: Wait; my ticket says Saturday.

partner.en: But today's Friday.

learner.hr: Znam. Mislila sam da sam kupila današnju izvedbu.
learner.en: I know. I thought I'd bought tonight's performance.

partner.hr: Jesmo li barem kupili isti dan?
partner.en: Did we at least book the same day?

learner.hr: Jesmo. I na tvojoj karti je isti datum.
learner.en: Yes. Your ticket has the same date too.

partner.en: Then we've got a free evening.

learner.hr: Imamo, i cijeli dan da prestanem paničariti.
learner.en: Yes, and a whole day for me to stop panicking.

partner.en: Shall we go somewhere anyway?

learner.hr: Hajdemo na pivo, kad smo se već spremili.
learner.en: Let's get a beer, since we're ready to go.

conversations.title: Not enough birthday candles

partner.en: How many candles have we got?

learner.hr: Devet, a torta je za nečiji četrdeseti rođendan.
learner.en: Nine, and the cake's for someone's fortieth birthday.

partner.en: Can we buy more?

learner.hr: Prekasno je. Trgovina je zatvorena.
learner.en: It's too late. The shop is closed.

partner.en: What shall we do, then?

learner.hr: Stavi četiri, neka svaka predstavlja deset godina.
learner.en: Put four on; let each one represent ten years.

partner.en: Do you think he'll be upset?

learner.hr: Neće. Više ga brine hoće li dobiti velik komad.
learner.en: No. He's more worried about getting a big slice.

partner.en: Four it is, then.

learner.hr: Dobro, samo ih nemoj ugasiti prije slavljenika.
learner.en: Good; just don't blow them out before the birthday boy.

conversations.title: A chair swap in the office

partner.en: Why are you sitting in my chair?

learner.hr: Nisam znao da je tvoja. Moja je nestala.
learner.en: I didn't know it was yours. Mine has disappeared.

partner.hr: Tvoja je u sobi za sastanke.
partner.en: Yours is in the meeting room.

learner.hr: Tko ju je odnio onamo bez pitanja?
learner.en: Who took it there without asking?

partner.en: Probably the people at this morning's meeting.

learner.hr: Onda ću je vratiti prije nego što je netko odnese dalje.
learner.en: Then I'll bring it back before someone moves it again.

partner.en: You can keep this one until then.

learner.hr: Hvala, ali neću dugo. Tvoja je previsoka za moj stol.
learner.en: Thanks, but not for long. Yours is too high for my desk.

partner.en: Maybe we should label the chairs.

learner.hr: Ili prestati uređivati ured kao igru glazbenih stolica.
learner.en: Or stop organising the office like a game of musical chairs.

conversations.title: A new mural on a familiar wall

partner.en: Have you seen the new mural?

learner.hr: Jesam. Onaj crni zid sad izgleda potpuno drukčije.
learner.en: Yes. That black wall looks completely different now.

partner.en: What do you think it shows?

learner.hr: Žene koje rade u staroj tvornici, barem mi tako izgleda.
learner.en: Women working in the old factory, at least that's how it looks to me.

partner.hr: Umjetnica je razgovarala s bivšim radnicama.
partner.en: The artist spoke to former workers.

learner.hr: Zato lica djeluju tako stvarno, a ne kao ukras.
learner.en: That's why the faces feel so real rather than decorative.

partner.en: Shall we look at it close up?

learner.hr: Hoćemo. Želim pročitati imena napisana uz rub.
learner.en: Yes. I want to read the names written along the edge.

partner.en: It's loveliest in the morning light.

learner.hr: Onda ćemo sutra proći ovuda prije posla.
learner.en: Then we'll come this way before work tomorrow.

conversations.title: An umbrella left at a café

partner.en: Why are you going back to the café?

learner.hr: Ostavio sam kišobran ispod našeg stola.
learner.en: I left my umbrella under our table.

partner.en: Are you sure it's there?

learner.hr: Nisam, ali posljednje ga se tamo sjećam.
learner.en: No, but that's the last place I remember it.

partner.en: I can wait for you here.

learner.hr: Idi radije naprijed. Ne moraš zbog mene kasniti.
learner.en: Go on ahead instead. You needn't be late because of me.

partner.en: Will you call me afterwards?

learner.hr: Hoću, čim saznam jesam li ga pronašao.
learner.en: Yes, as soon as I know whether I've found it.

partner.hr: Nadam se da ćeš imati sreće.
partner.en: I hope you have some luck.

learner.hr: I ja. To je već treći kišobran ove jeseni.
learner.en: So do I. It's already my third umbrella this autumn.

conversations.title: Who gets the window seat?

partner.en: You want the window seat again?

learner.hr: Da, ali znam da je ovaj put red na tebe.
learner.en: Yes, but I know it's your turn this time.

partner.hr: Možemo se zamijeniti na pola puta.
partner.en: We can swap halfway through.

learner.hr: Može. Samo nemoj reći da je pola tek pred dolazak.
learner.en: Yes. Just don't say halfway is right before we arrive.

partner.en: We'll agree on a specific station.

learner.hr: Dobro. Do tada ću gledati kroz tvoj prozor.
learner.en: Good. Until then I'll look out through your window.

partner.en: Just don't block my view.

learner.hr: Neću. Ruksak ću staviti gore da imamo više mjesta.
learner.en: I won't. I'll put my backpack up so we've got more room.

partner.en: There, we can agree after all.

learner.hr: Možemo, dok se ne počnemo dogovarati oko zadnjeg sendviča.
learner.en: We can, until we start negotiating over the last sandwich.

conversations.title: A spare key before a holiday

partner.hr: Možeš li čuvati naš rezervni ključ?
partner.en: Can you keep our spare key?

learner.hr: Mogu. Želite li da i povremeno otvorim prozore?
learner.en: Yes. Would you also like me to open the windows occasionally?

partner.en: No need; just water the plants.

learner.hr: Dobro. Koliko često zalijevate ovu veliku biljku?
learner.en: All right. How often do you water this big plant?

partner.en: I'll leave written instructions.

learner.hr: Odlično. Tako neću pomiješati vaše navike s mojima.
learner.en: Great. That way I won't confuse your routine with mine.

partner.en: We'll be back in a week.

learner.hr: Javite ako se plan promijeni, da znam do kada dolazim.
learner.en: Let me know if the plan changes so I know how long to keep coming.

partner.en: Thank you; you've saved us.

learner.hr: Nema na čemu. Samo mi ostavite ključ koji stvarno otvara vrata.
learner.en: You're welcome. Just leave me a key that actually opens the door.

conversations.title: A banknote in a museum drawer

partner.en: What's in this drawer?

learner.hr: Stari novac. Ovdje vidim funte, a tamo dolare. Tu je i dolar s drukčijim portretom. Britanski novac držali su u zasebnoj kutiji.
learner.en: Old money. I can see pounds here and dollars there. There is also a dollar with a different portrait here. They kept British money in a separate box.

partner.en: How much is this banknote worth?

learner.hr: Na njoj piše deset dolara, ali više se ne koristi.
learner.en: It says ten dollars, but it isn't used anymore.

partner.en: Why do they keep it, then?

learner.hr: Zbog priče koju nosi, ne zbog kupnje.
learner.en: For the story it carries, not for spending.

partner.en: Who brought it?

learner.hr: Piše da ju je darovao pomorac iz našeg grada.
learner.en: It says a sailor from our city donated it.

partner.en: Can we see the other side?

learner.hr: Možemo na ekranu. Izvornik ne smijemo dirati.
learner.en: On the screen, yes. We mustn't touch the original.

conversations.title: An ending that does not fit a novel

partner.hr: Je li ti se svidio završetak?
partner.en: Did you like the ending?

learner.hr: Ne baš. Junak pobjegne iz zatvora bez ikakvog objašnjenja.
learner.en: Not really. The hero escapes from prison without any explanation.

partner.en: Maybe the writer wanted a surprise.

learner.hr: Iznenađenje nije isto što i rupa u priči.
learner.en: A surprise isn't the same as a hole in the story.

partner.en: What would you change?

learner.hr: Vratio bih lik odvjetnika koji je nestao na polovici.
learner.en: I'd bring back the lawyer character who disappeared halfway through.

partner.en: To help him prove his innocence?

learner.hr: Upravo to. Sloboda bi onda imala smislen uzrok.
learner.en: Exactly. His freedom would then have a meaningful cause.

partner.en: Will you read the sequel?

learner.hr: Hoću, ali ovaj put imam manja očekivanja.
learner.en: Yes, but this time my expectations are lower.

conversations.title: A suspect in two places at once

partner.en: Why did you rewind the film?

learner.hr: Osumnjičeni je upravo rekao da je cijelu večer bio doma.
learner.en: The suspect just said he was home all evening.

partner.en: Wasn't he in the bar?

learner.hr: Jest. Vidjeli smo ga prije scene ubojstva.
learner.en: Yes. We saw him before the murder scene.

partner.hr: Možda detektiv to još ne zna.
partner.en: Maybe the detective doesn't know that yet.

learner.hr: Onda konobarica može potvrditi njegovu laž.
learner.en: Then the waitress can confirm he's lying.

partner.en: Do you think he's the murderer?

learner.hr: Ne nužno. Možda skriva neku drugu tajnu.
learner.en: Not necessarily. Maybe he's hiding another secret.

partner.en: Shall we keep watching?

learner.hr: Hoćemo. Samo nemoj unaprijed pročitati tko je kriv.
learner.en: Yes. Just don't read ahead to find out who's guilty.

conversations.title: Disliking a convincing character

partner.hr: Zašto kažeš da je knjiga dobra?
partner.en: Why do you say the book is good?

learner.hr: Zato što je uvjerljiva, iako je glavni lik grozan.
learner.en: Because it's convincing, even though the main character is awful.

partner.en: He keeps lying to his wife.

learner.hr: Znam. Njegova supruga jedina primjećuje koliko se promijenio.
learner.en: I know. His wife is the only one who notices how much he's changed.

partner.en: Do you think he deserves forgiveness?

learner.hr: Ne znam. Morao bi prvo priznati što je učinio.
learner.en: I don't know. He'd need to admit what he'd done first.

partner.en: He leaves in the end, though.

learner.hr: Da, a njegov odlazak ne rješava njezine probleme.
learner.en: Yes, and his departure doesn't solve her problems.

partner.hr: Baš nas je potaknula na raspravu.
partner.en: It certainly prompted a discussion.

learner.hr: Jest. Draža mi je takva knjiga nego savršeni junaci.
learner.en: Yes. I prefer a book like that to perfect heroes.

conversations.title: One missing jigsaw piece

partner.en: Is the jigsaw finally finished?

learner.hr: Gotova je osim jednog dijela, baš na sredini neba.
learner.en: Apart from one piece, right in the middle of the sky.

partner.en: Have you looked under the table?

learner.hr: Jesam. Našla sam prašinu i jednu izgubljenu naušnicu.
learner.en: Yes. I found dust and a lost earring.

partner.en: Maybe the cat took the piece.

learner.hr: Moguće. Obožava gurati stvari šapom preko ruba.
learner.en: Possibly. She loves pushing things over the edge with her paw.

partner.en: There's something under the rug.

learner.hr: To je on! Nebo napokon opet ima smisla.
